tools.description: Get orthologous genes from an OrthoDB group, optionally filtered by species. Returns gene IDs, organism names, and descriptions for all members of an orthologous group. Useful for finding orthologs across species, evolutionary conservation analysis, and functional annotation transfer. Example: group '727649at7742' with species=9606 returns human genes in that orthologous group.

group_id.description: OrthoDB group ID. Format: 'numberATtaxid'. Get IDs from OrthoDB_search_groups.

species.description: Comma-separated NCBI taxonomy IDs to filter. Examples: '9606' (human only), '9606,10090' (human+mouse). Null for all species.

tools.name: OrthoDB_search_groups
tools.summary: Searches OrthoDB v12 orthologous groups by gene/protein name and taxonomic level.
tools.description: Search for orthologous groups by gene/protein name in OrthoDB v12. OrthoDB catalogs orthologous groups at different taxonomic levels (vertebrates, metazoa, eukaryotes, etc.), enabling evolutionary analysis of gene conservation. Returns group IDs that can be queried for details. Complements OMA and Ensembl Compara with group-level orthology at deep evolutionary scales. Example: searching 'BRCA1' with species=9606 returns orthologous groups containing BRCA1 at various taxonomic levels.

query.description: Gene or protein name to search. Examples: 'BRCA1', 'TP53', 'insulin', 'EGFR'.

species.description: NCBI taxonomy ID to filter by species. Examples: 9606 (human), 10090 (mouse), 7227 (fly). Null for all species.

level.description: Taxonomic level for group definition. Examples: 7742 (Vertebrata), 33208 (Metazoa), 2759 (Eukaryota). Null for all levels.

limit.description: Maximum number of groups to return (1-50). Default: 10.

tools.name: PANTHER_enrichment
tools.summary: Runs PANTHER overrepresentation analysis on a gene list for GO terms, pathways or protein classes.
tools.description: Perform gene set enrichment (overrepresentation) analysis using PANTHER. Given a gene list, identifies statistically enriched GO terms, PANTHER pathways, Reactome pathways, or protein classes using Fisher's exact test with FDR correction. PANTHER is one of the most widely used tools for functional enrichment in bioinformatics. Example: gene list 'TP53,BRCA1,EGFR,KRAS,PTEN' enriched for GO biological_process returns 'regulation of mitotic cell cycle phase transition' (FDR=0.003).

gene_list.description: Comma-separated list of gene symbols, UniProt IDs, or Ensembl IDs. Example: 'TP53,BRCA1,EGFR,KRAS,PTEN,APC,RB1'.

organism.description: NCBI taxonomy ID. Default: 9606 (human). Others: 10090 (mouse), 7227 (fly), 559292 (yeast).

annotation_dataset.description: Annotation dataset for enrichment. Options: 'GO:0008150' (biological_process, default), 'GO:0003674' (molecular_function), 'GO:0005575' (cellular_component), 'ANNOT_TYPE_ID_PANTHER_PATHWAY' (PANTHER pathway), 'ANNOT_TYPE_ID_REACTOME_PATHWAY' (Reactome pathway), 'ANNOT_TYPE_ID_PANTHER_PC' (protein class).

tools.name: PANTHER_gene_info
tools.summary: Returns PANTHER family/subfamily, GO annotations and protein class for a gene.
tools.description: Get gene classification and functional annotation from PANTHER (Protein ANalysis THrough Evolutionary Relationships). Returns PANTHER family/subfamily, Gene Ontology annotations (molecular function, biological process, cellular component), PANTHER protein class, and pathway membership. PANTHER classifies genes by evolutionary relationships across 144 organisms. Example: P04637 returns TP53 classified in family PTHR11447 (tumor protein p53) with GO annotations for DNA-binding transcription factor activity.

gene_id.description: Gene identifier - UniProt accession, Ensembl ID, or gene symbol. Examples: 'P04637' (TP53), 'P38398' (BRCA1), 'ENSG00000141510'.

organism.description: NCBI taxonomy ID. Default: 9606 (human). Others: 10090 (mouse), 10116 (rat), 7227 (fly), 6239 (worm), 559292 (yeast).

tools.name: PANTHER_ortholog
tools.summary: Finds orthologs of a gene across species using PANTHER, with ortholog type.
tools.description: Find orthologs of a gene across species using PANTHER evolutionary classification. Returns EVERY matching ortholog in 'mappings' (count in 'total_mappings'), each with its persistent ID, gene symbol, and ortholog type (LDO=Least Diverged Ortholog, O=ortholog, P=paralog, X=xenolog, LDX=least diverged xenolog); 'mapping' repeats the first entry for backward compatibility and is not the whole answer. A gene often has several orthologs in one target species -- human ABCB1 maps to both mouse Abcb1a (LDO) and Abcb1b (O) -- so read 'mappings', especially with ortholog_type='O'. PANTHER classifies orthologs by evolutionary divergence across 144 fully sequenced genomes. Example: P04637 (human TP53) maps to Tp53 (mouse P02340) as LDO.

gene_id.description: Gene identifier - UniProt accession, Ensembl ID, or gene symbol. Examples: 'P04637' (TP53), 'P38398' (BRCA1).

organism.description: Source organism NCBI taxonomy ID. Default: 9606 (human).

target_organism.description: Target organism NCBI taxonomy ID. Default: 10090 (mouse). Others: 10116 (rat), 7227 (fly), 6239 (worm).

ortholog_type.description: Ortholog type filter. Options: 'LDO' (least diverged ortholog, default), 'O' (all orthologs), 'P' (paralogs), 'X' (xenologs), 'LDX' (least diverged xenolog), 'all' (all types).

tools.name: PDC_get_gene_protein
tools.summary: Returns gene description, NCBI gene ID, protein accessions and PDC study coverage for a gene symbol.
tools.description: Get protein information and proteomics study coverage for a gene from the NCI Proteomics Data Commons (PDC). Given a gene symbol (e.g., TP53, EGFR, MYC), returns the gene description, NCBI gene ID, HGNC authority, associated protein accessions (UniProt, RefSeq, Ensembl), and spectral count data across all PDC studies where the protein was detected. Spectral counts indicate protein abundance evidence in each study. Useful for understanding which cancer proteomics datasets have measured a specific protein.

gene_name.description: Gene symbol to look up (e.g., 'TP53', 'EGFR', 'BRCA1', 'MYC')

tools.name: PGSCatalog_get_performance_metrics
tools.summary: Returns published evaluation metrics (OR, HR, AUC, sample sets) for a PGS Catalog score.
tools.description: Retrieve the published validation/evaluation performance metrics for a polygenic score from the PGS Catalog by its PGS id (e.g. 'PGS000001'). Returns one record per evaluation sample set, each with: effect sizes (Odds Ratio OR, Hazard Ratio HR, beta), classification accuracy (AUROC, Concordance/C-index), and other metrics (R2, top-vs-bottom quantile OR) — each as an estimate with 95% CI (ci_lower/ci_upper) — plus the evaluation cohort ancestry (ancestry_broad/free/country) and sample size (sample_number, cases, controls), covariates, and source publication. Use this to judge how well a score predicts and in which ancestries it was validated. Find PGS ids with PGSCatalog_get_scores_by_trait. No API key.

pgs_id.description: PGS Catalog score id, e.g. 'PGS000001' or 'PGS000004'.

tools.name: PGSCatalog_get_score
tools.summary: Returns metadata of a PGS Catalog polygenic score: traits, variant count, method, build and ancestry.
tools.description: Retrieve the full metadata for a specific polygenic score from the PGS Catalog by its PGS id (e.g. 'PGS000001'): reported and EFO/MONDO traits, number of variants, development method, genome build, weight type, publication, training samples, ancestry distribution, and the downloadable scoring-file URL. Find PGS ids with PGSCatalog_get_scores_by_trait. No API key.

tools.name: PGSCatalog_get_scores_by_trait
tools.summary: Lists published polygenic scores for an EFO/MONDO trait from the PGS Catalog.
tools.description: List the published polygenic scores (PGS) for a trait in the PGS Catalog, given its EFO/MONDO trait id (find one with PGSCatalog_search_traits). Each score summary includes the PGS id, name, reported trait, number of variants, development method, genome build, and publication (author/journal/year/PMID/DOI) plus the scoring-file URL. Use PGSCatalog_get_score for the full record of one score. No API key.

trait_id.description: EFO or MONDO trait id, e.g. 'MONDO_0004989' (breast carcinoma) or 'EFO_0001645' (coronary artery disease).

tools.name: PGSCatalog_search_traits
tools.summary: Searches PGS Catalog traits by term and returns trait IDs with polygenic score counts.
tools.description: Search the PGS Catalog (pgscatalog.org, EMBL-EBI — the open database of published polygenic scores) for traits/phenotypes matching a term. Returns each matching trait's id (EFO/MONDO, e.g. 'MONDO_0004989'), label, description, and the number of polygenic scores published for it. Use this first to find the trait_id, then PGSCatalog_get_scores_by_trait to list its scores. No API key.

query.description: Trait or phenotype term, e.g. 'coronary artery disease', 'type 2 diabetes', 'breast cancer'. PGS Catalog's own search can return zero results for some multi-word phrases that don't exactly match an indexed label even when a near-identical trait exists (e.g. 'familial hypercholesterolemia' finds nothing while 'hypercholesterolemia' alone does) -- if a natural-language query returns no results, retry with a shorter or more generic core term.

tools.name: PanelApp_get_panel
tools.summary: Returns all genes in a Genomics England PanelApp panel with confidence level, inheritance mode and phenotypes.
tools.description: Get the full gene list and details for a specific Genomics England PanelApp gene panel by panel ID. Returns all genes in the panel with their confidence levels (3=green/diagnostic, 2=amber/borderline, 1=red/limited), mode of inheritance, mode of pathogenicity, penetrance, phenotypes, publications, and evidence sources. This is the definitive resource for which genes are included in clinical genetic testing panels used by the NHS. Use PanelApp_search_panels to find panel IDs.

panel_id.description: PanelApp panel ID (e.g., 504 for 'Inherited polyposis and early onset colorectal cancer'). Find IDs using PanelApp_search_panels.

tools.name: PanelApp_search_genes
tools.summary: Lists PanelApp panels containing a gene, with confidence level, inheritance and phenotypes.
tools.description: Search for a gene across all Genomics England PanelApp panels to find which clinical testing panels include it. Returns all panels containing the gene, along with the confidence level, mode of inheritance, and associated phenotypes for each panel. This is invaluable for understanding the clinical significance of a gene - if it appears in multiple high-confidence panels, it has strong clinical evidence. Use gene symbols (e.g., 'TP53', 'BRCA1').

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol to search across all panels (e.g., 'TP53', 'BRCA1', 'EGFR', 'MLH1')

tools.name: PanelApp_search_panels
tools.summary: Searches Genomics England PanelApp gene panels by name or disease group.
tools.description: Search Genomics England PanelApp for gene panels used in clinical genetic testing. PanelApp is the authoritative source for curated gene panels used by the NHS and global genomic medicine services. Returns panel IDs, names, disease groups, status, version, and gene count statistics. Use this to find relevant gene panels for a disease area, then use PanelApp_get_panel to get the full gene list. Panels contain genes with confidence levels (green=3 for diagnostic grade, amber=2 for borderline, red=1 for limited evidence). Matches only against panel-level metadata (name/disease group), not gene-level phenotype text, so some disease names (e.g. 'haemophilia') won't match any panel directly even though a relevant panel exists -- if a disease-name search returns nothing, try PanelApp_search_genes with the causal gene symbol instead (e.g. F8, F9 for haemophilia).

search.description: Search query for panel name or disease (e.g., 'breast cancer', 'epilepsy', 'hearing loss', 'intellectual disability')

tools.name: PanglaoDB_cell_types_for_gene
tools.summary: Lists cell types for which a gene is a curated PanglaoDB marker, with sensitivity/specificity.
tools.description: Reverse cell-type lookup for a gene using PanglaoDB (panglaodb.se). Given an official human gene symbol (e.g. 'CD19', 'ALB', 'EPCAM'), return every cell type for which that gene is a curated marker, with organ, canonical-marker flag, and per-gene sensitivity/specificity for human and mouse. Use this to interpret a marker gene found in a scRNA-seq cluster (e.g. 'which cell type does CD19 indicate?'). Optionally filter by species ('human' or 'mouse'). Results are sorted by descending human specificity. Note: the marker set is the frozen 2020 PanglaoDB release (no longer updated) — reliable for canonical markers, but not for cell types/markers described since.

gene.description: Official human gene symbol, e.g. 'CD19', 'ALB', 'EPCAM', 'INS'. Case-insensitive. Required.

species.description: Optional species filter: 'human' (Hs) or 'mouse' (Mm). If omitted, returns all species.

limit.description: Maximum number of cell-type records to return. Default 50.

tools.name: PanglaoDB_markers_for_cell_type
tools.summary: Returns curated PanglaoDB marker genes for a cell type with sensitivity/specificity for human and mouse.
tools.description: Get curated marker genes for a single-cell type from PanglaoDB (panglaodb.se). Returns marker genes used to annotate scRNA-seq clusters, each with canonical-marker flag, ubiquitousness index, and per-gene sensitivity/specificity for human and mouse. Useful for cell-type annotation and validating cluster identity. cell_type must match a PanglaoDB cell-type label (use PanglaoDB_list_cell_types to discover them; examples: 'B cells', 'Hepatocytes', 'T cells', 'Macrophages'). Optionally filter by species ('human' or 'mouse'), organ, or canonical_only. Results are sorted canonical-first, then by descending human specificity. Note: the marker set is the frozen 2020 PanglaoDB release (no longer updated) — reliable for canonical markers, but not for cell types/markers described since.

cell_type.description: PanglaoDB cell-type label, e.g. 'B cells', 'Hepatocytes', 'T cells'. Case-insensitive exact match. Required.

species.description: Optional species filter: 'human' (Hs) or 'mouse' (Mm). If omitted, returns markers for all species.

organ.description: Optional organ filter, e.g. 'Liver', 'Immune system', 'Pancreas'. Case-insensitive exact match.

canonical_only.description: If true, return only canonical marker genes. Default false.

limit.description: Maximum number of marker genes to return. Default 50.

tools.name: Pathoplexus_count_sequences
tools.summary: Counts and aggregates open pathogen genome sequences in Pathoplexus by country, lineage or other fields.
tools.description: Count and aggregate open pathogen genome sequences in Pathoplexus (LAPIS) for genomic-epidemiology surveillance of emerging pathogens. Returns sequence counts for an organism, optionally filtered by country and lineage and grouped by a metadata field (e.g. geoLocCountry, lineage, sampleCollectionDate) to see geographic/temporal distribution. Known organisms: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf' (Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever), 'mpox'. No API key required.

organism.description: Pathoplexus organism slug: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'.

group_by.description: Metadata field to group counts by, e.g. 'geoLocCountry', 'lineage', 'sampleCollectionDate'.

tools.name: Pathoplexus_get_mutations
tools.summary: Returns characteristic nucleotide or amino-acid mutations for a Pathoplexus organism above a proportion threshold.
tools.description: Get characteristic amino-acid (default) or nucleotide mutations for a Pathoplexus organism above a proportion threshold, optionally filtered by country/lineage — for surveillance of mutation prevalence in emerging pathogens. Returns each mutation with gene, position, from/to residue, proportion (fraction of sequences carrying it), count, and coverage. Known organisms: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'. No API key required.

organism.description: Pathoplexus organism slug, e.g. 'west-nile', 'mpox'.

min_proportion.description: Minimum proportion of sequences carrying the mutation (default 0.8).

limit.description: Max mutations (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: Pathoplexus_get_sequence_details
tools.summary: Lists per-sequence metadata records (accession, country, date, host, lineage) for a Pathoplexus organism.
tools.description: List the individual sequence records (not aggregated counts) behind a Pathoplexus organism, from the LAPIS /details endpoint. Returns a per-sequence metadata table — accession, country (geoLocCountry), collection date (sampleCollectionDate), host, lineage, clade and any other requested fields — so you can enumerate the actual surveilled genomes rather than only their totals. Optionally filter by country and lineage and select which fields to return. Known organisms: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'. No API key required.

organism.description: Pathoplexus organism slug: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'.

fields.description: Comma-separated metadata fields to return, e.g. 'accession,geoLocCountry,sampleCollectionDate,lineage'. Omit to return all available fields.

limit.description: Max sequence rows (default 50, max 1000).

offset.description: Row offset for pagination (default 0).

tools.name: Pathoplexus_get_sequences_fasta
tools.summary: Downloads unaligned or aligned nucleotide or amino-acid FASTA sequences for a Pathoplexus organism.
tools.description: Download the actual genome sequences (FASTA) from Pathoplexus/LAPIS for a surveilled pathogen. Returns unaligned (default) or aligned nucleotide or amino-acid sequences as FASTA text, optionally filtered by country and lineage. This is the only way in ToolUniverse to retrieve the nucleotide/protein sequence of Pathoplexus genomes — the other tools expose only counts and mutations. Known organisms: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'. No API key required.

organism.description: Pathoplexus organism slug: 'west-nile', 'ebola-zaire', 'ebola-sudan', 'cchf', 'mpox'.

aligned.description: Return aligned sequences instead of unaligned (default false).

limit.description: Number of sequences to download (default 1, max 100).

tools.name: PathwayCommons_get_neighborhood
tools.summary: Returns known interactions (PPI, regulatory, catalytic) for a gene from Pathway Commons.
tools.description: Get the interaction neighborhood for a gene from Pathway Commons. Returns all known interactions (protein-protein, regulatory, catalytic, complex membership) for the query gene from 22 integrated databases. Each interaction includes the partner gene, interaction type (interacts-with, controls-state-change-of, controls-expression-of, in-complex-with, etc.), data source, and PubMed references. Useful for building gene interaction networks and finding functional partners.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g., BRCA1, TP53, EGFR)

limit.description: Graph search depth (1 = direct neighbors, 2 = neighbors of neighbors). Default 1. Higher values return much more data.

datasource.description: Filter by data source: reactome, kegg, biogrid, intact, hprd, pid, corum, ctd, drugbank

max_results.description: Maximum number of interactions to return (default: 100)

tools.name: PathwayCommons_get_pathway
tools.summary: Returns a Pathway Commons pathway by URI with its name, participants and interaction processes.
tools.description: Get detailed pathway information from Pathway Commons by URI. Returns the pathway name, participants (proteins, small molecules, complexes), and processes (interactions, catalysis, controls). Use URIs from PathwayCommons_search results. Covers Reactome, KEGG, WikiPathways, PID, and other sources. Response is parsed from BioPAX/JSON-LD format.

uri.description: Pathway Commons URI from search results, e.g., http://bioregistry.io/reactome:R-HSA-5693532 (DNA Double-Strand Break Repair)

tools.name: PathwayCommons_paths_between
tools.summary: Finds mechanistic interaction paths between two or more gene symbols across Pathway Commons sources.
tools.description: Find mechanistic interaction paths connecting a set of genes/proteins in Pathway Commons (PC2 kind=PATHSBETWEEN across 22 integrated databases: Reactome, KEGG, WikiPathways, PID, BioGRID, IntAct, etc.). Given two or more gene symbols, returns the directed/undirected interaction edges that link them, parsed from SIF triples into {source, relation, target}. Relations include in-complex-with, controls-state-change-of, controls-phosphorylation-of, controls-expression-of, chemical-affects, used-to-produce. Use to reveal how a gene set is mechanistically connected (e.g. a DNA-repair module BRCA1/BRCA2/TP53). Requires at least 2 distinct genes. Note: an uncached query can be slow; if it times out, retry (results are cached server-side).

genes.description: Two or more gene symbols / identifiers to connect, e.g. ["BRCA1", "BRCA2", "TP53"]. A comma-separated string is also accepted.

limit.description: Path length limit (graph search distance). Default 1 (direct mechanistic links). Higher values include longer indirect paths and much more data.

datasource.description: Filter by data source: reactome, kegg, biogrid, intact, hprd, pid, corum, ctd, drugbank

max_results.description: Maximum number of edges to return (default: 200)

tools.name: PharmGKB_get_clinical_annotations
tools.summary: Returns PharmGKB clinical annotations with variant-level gene-drug-phenotype significance by annotation ID.
tools.description: Get clinical annotations showing gene-drug-phenotype relationships. Returns variant-level clinical significance data. Always provide annotation_id — gene_id lookup is not supported by the API and returns an error with guidance.

annotation_id.description: PharmGKB clinical annotation ID (e.g., '1447954390'). Required for reliable results.

gene_id.description: PharmGKB Gene Accession ID (e.g., "PA128"). NOTE: Gene-based lookup is not supported — will return an error with instructions to use annotation_id instead.

gene.description: NOT SUPPORTED: PharmGKB API requires a specific annotation_id (e.g. "1447954390"), not a gene symbol. Browse https://www.pharmgkb.org/clinicalAnnotation to find annotation IDs. For gene-drug dosing use CPIC_list_guidelines instead.

gene_symbol.description: Alias for gene — NOT SUPPORTED. See gene parameter.

tools.name: PharmGKB_get_dosing_guidelines
tools.summary: Returns CPIC/DPWG pharmacogenetic dosing guidelines from PharmGKB by guideline ID.
tools.description: Get pharmacogenetic dosing guidelines (CPIC/DPWG) from PharmGKB by guideline_id. IMPORTANT: use the 'clinpgxid' field from CPIC_list_guidelines (e.g., 'PA166251454'), NOT the 'pharmgkbid' field — old-format pharmgkbid values (e.g., 'PA166104996') return HTTP 404. The test example PA166251465 is for the warfarin guideline.

guideline_id.description: PharmGKB ClinPGx guideline ID from CPIC_list_guidelines 'clinpgxid' field (e.g., 'PA166251465' for warfarin, 'PA166251454' for opioids/codeine, 'PA166251458' for tamoxifen). Use clinpgxid, NOT pharmgkbid.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g., 'CYP2D6'). NOTE: Filtering by gene symbol is unreliable and may return a generic prompt instead of actual guidelines. Use guideline_id instead.

tools.name: PharmGKB_get_gene_details
tools.summary: Returns chromosomal location and cross-references for a PharmGKB gene accession.
tools.description: Get detailed information for a gene using its PharmGKB Accession ID. Returns chromosomal location, cross-references, and other metadata.

gene_id.description: PharmGKB Gene Accession ID (e.g., 'PA128').

tools.name: PharmGKB_get_variant_annotations
tools.summary: Returns PharmGKB variant annotations (allele/genotype, phenotype, significance) filtered by gene or chemical.
tools.description: Get variant-level literature annotations from PharmGKB/ClinPGx, filtered by gene or chemical PharmGKB Accession ID. Provide gene_id (e.g., 'PA126' for CYP2C9) OR chemical_id (e.g., 'PA451906' for warfarin). Each annotation gives allele/genotype, phenotype category, drug context, significance, and source literature. Results are capped by 'limit'. Keyless. Resolve gene/drug names to PA IDs first via PharmGKB_search_genes / PharmGKB_search_drugs.

gene_id.description: PharmGKB Gene Accession ID (e.g., 'PA126' for CYP2C9). Queried via location.genes.accessionId. Provide either gene_id or chemical_id.

chemical_id.description: PharmGKB Chemical/drug Accession ID (e.g., 'PA451906' for warfarin). Queried via relatedChemicals.accessionId. Provide either gene_id or chemical_id.

limit.description: Maximum number of variant annotations to return (default 50, max 500). CYP2C9 alone has over 1000 annotations.

tools.name: PharmGKB_search_genes
tools.summary: Searches PharmGKB genes by name, symbol or ID.
tools.description: Search for genes in PharmGKB by name, symbol, or ID. Returns PharmGKB Gene ID and basic gene metadata.

query.description: Gene name, symbol, or PharmGKB Accession ID (e.g., 'CYP2D6', 'PA128').

tools.name: PharmGKB_search_variants
tools.summary: Searches PharmGKB genetic variants by rsID or name with gene info.
tools.description: Search for genetic variants in PharmGKB by rsID or name. Returns variant IDs and associated gene info.

query.description: Variant name or rsID (e.g., 'rs1799853').

tools.name: PharmVar_get_alleles
tools.summary: Returns PharmVar star allele definitions, function, activity scores and variant details for a pharmacogene.
tools.description: Get all allele definitions for a pharmacogene from PharmVar (Pharmacogene Variation Consortium). Returns star allele names (e.g., CYP2D6*1, *4, *17), functional status, activity scores, variant details (HGVS notation, rsIDs, genomic positions), and evidence levels. PharmVar is the authoritative source for pharmacogenomic star allele nomenclature used in CPIC guidelines.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g., 'CYP2D6', 'CYP2C9', 'CYP2C19', 'CYP2B6', 'DPYD', 'SLCO1B1', 'UGT1A1', 'VKORC1')

tools.name: PharmVar_list_genes
tools.summary: Lists pharmacogenes curated by PharmVar.
tools.description: List all pharmacogenes curated by PharmVar (Pharmacogene Variation Consortium). PharmVar is the authoritative repository for pharmacogene allele nomenclature and variant data, defining star (*) alleles for genes like CYP2D6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2B6, and DPYD. Returns 15+ genes with their allele counts and descriptions.

tools.name: PharmacoDB_get_biomarker_assoc
tools.summary: Returns gene-compound biomarker associations linking gene expression or mutation to drug sensitivity.
tools.description: Get gene-compound biomarker associations from PharmacoDB showing how gene expression or other molecular features correlate with drug sensitivity. Returns statistical associations including effect estimate, p-values, FDR, sensitivity statistic (AAC/IC50), molecular data type (rna/cnv/mutation), sample size, and tissue/dataset context. Filter by compound, gene (Ensembl ID), tissue, and molecular data type. Useful for pharmacogenomics biomarker discovery and validating drug sensitivity predictors. Example: find genes associated with Paclitaxel sensitivity in breast cancer.

compound_name.description: Compound name (e.g., 'Paclitaxel', 'Erlotinib'). Either compound_name or compound_id required.

compound_id.description: PharmacoDB compound ID. Either compound_name or compound_id required.

gene_name.description: Gene Ensembl ID to filter (e.g., 'ENSG00000141510' for TP53)

per_page.description: Number of results per page (default 20, max 100)

tools.name: PharmacoDB_get_molecular_profiling
tools.summary: Lists which molecular profiling data types (RNA-seq, mutation, CNV) exist for a cell line and in which dataset.
tools.description: Get the per-cell-line molecular profiling inventory from PharmacoDB: which molecular data types (e.g., Kallisto RNA-seq isoforms, rnaseq, rna microarray, mutation, cnv) are available for a given cancer cell line, and in which pharmacogenomics dataset (CCLE, CTRPv2, FIMM, GDSC1/2, gCSI, etc.), with the number of profiles available (num_prof). Use this to confirm a cell line has the omics layer you need before pulling biomarker associations. Look up by cell_line_name (e.g., 'MCF-7') or cell_line_id. Example: cell_line_name='MCF-7' (cell id 273) returns records like {dataset CCLE, mDataType 'Kallisto_0.46.1.rnaseq', num_prof 1} plus mutation/cnv/rna layers.

cell_line_name.description: Cancer cell line name (e.g., 'MCF-7', 'A549'). Mutually exclusive with cell_line_id.

cell_line_id.description: PharmacoDB cell line database ID (e.g., 273 for MCF-7). Mutually exclusive with cell_line_name.

tools.name: Pharos_get_disease_targets
tools.summary: Returns Pharos targets associated with a disease with Target Development Level filtering.
tools.description: Get drug targets associated with a disease from Pharos. Returns targets with TDL classification to identify druggable vs understudied proteins for the disease. Supports TDL filtering to find Tdark opportunities.

tdl.description: Optional filter by Target Development Level

tools.name: Pharos_get_target
tools.summary: Returns Pharos target details (TDL, family, novelty, diseases) by gene symbol or UniProt ID.
tools.description: Get detailed drug target information from Pharos/TCRD by gene symbol or UniProt ID. Returns Target Development Level (Tdark/Tbio/Tchem/Tclin -- Pharos' druggability classification), protein family, novelty score, publication count, associated diseases (full per-disease association counts plus the top 10 diseases with MONDO IDs), and ligand/drug counts plus the top 10 ligands. Essential for identifying understudied proteins. For ligand bioactivity values use Pharos_get_target_ligands.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g., 'EGFR', 'TP53', 'BRCA1'). Use either gene or uniprot.

uniprot.description: UniProt accession (e.g., 'P00533'). Use either gene or uniprot.

tools.name: Pharos_get_target_expression
tools.summary: Returns GTEx per-tissue TPM expression for a target gene from Pharos.
tools.description: Get GTEx baseline tissue RNA expression (per-tissue TPM) for a drug target from Pharos/TCRD (by gene symbol or UniProt ID). Returns one record per GTEx tissue with tissue name, TPM value, and gender stratification when available. Use to assess where a target is naturally expressed (e.g., for on-target tissue-toxicity reasoning).

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g., 'DRD2', 'EGFR'). Use either gene or uniprot.

uniprot.description: UniProt accession (e.g., 'P14416'). Use either gene or uniprot.

tools.name: PlantReactome_get_pathway_participants
tools.summary: Lists gene and protein participants with UniProt accessions and gene names for a Plant Reactome pathway.
tools.description: List the gene/protein/molecule participants of a Plant Reactome pathway or reaction (the macromolecules that are IN the pathway), with UniProt accessions and gene names. PlantReactome_get_pathway returns only pathway metadata and 'hasEvent' sub-event IDs, not the participant gene products; use this tool to get the actual genes/proteins. Each participant carries its refEntities, where 'identifier' is the UniProt accession and 'gene_names' lists the gene symbols. Example: R-OSA-1119263 (Arginine biosynthesis, rice) returns 36 participants; the first refEntity is UniProt Q10MK5 with gene names including LOC_OS03G19280. No API key required.

pathway_id.description: Plant Reactome stable identifier of a pathway or reaction. Format: R-{species_code}-{number}. Example: 'R-OSA-1119263' (Arginine biosynthesis in rice).

tools.name: Planteome_search_annotations
tools.summary: Returns GO, PO and TO annotations for a plant gene from Planteome.
tools.description: Search Planteome's gene-to-ontology-term annotation index by gene id or accession. Resolves a plant gene to every ontology term (GO/PO/TO/crop ontologies) it has been annotated with, across evidence types and source databases. Example: query='AT4G32150' (Arabidopsis VAMP711) returns its GO annotations including 'vesicle-mediated transport'.

query.description: Gene id or accession, e.g. 'AT4G32150'.

limit.description: Max annotations to return, 1-100. Default 20.

tools.name: PomBase_get_gene
tools.summary: Returns PomBase gene details: name, product, domains, deletion viability and UniProt cross-reference.
tools.description: Get detailed gene information from PomBase for fission yeast (S. pombe) by systematic ID. Returns gene name, protein product, InterPro domain annotations, deletion viability, UniProt cross-reference, and transmembrane domain coordinates. S. pombe is a key model organism for cell cycle, chromosome biology, and RNA processing research. Example: SPBC11B10.09 returns cdc2 (cyclin-dependent kinase), essential for cell division.

gene_id.description: PomBase systematic gene identifier. Examples: 'SPBC11B10.09' (cdc2), 'SPAC2F7.03c' (pom1), 'SPAC1002.17c' (ase1).

tools.name: PomBase_get_gene_phenotypes
tools.summary: Returns FYPO phenotype annotations and deletion viability for an S. pombe gene.
tools.description: Get phenotype annotations for a fission yeast (S. pombe) gene from PomBase. Returns deletion viability, FYPO (Fission Yeast Phenotype Ontology) term annotations with evidence codes. S. pombe phenotypes are a key resource for understanding gene function in cell biology. Example: SPBC11B10.09 (cdc2) is inviable when deleted, reflecting its essential role in cell division.

gene_id.description: PomBase systematic gene identifier. Examples: 'SPBC11B10.09' (cdc2), 'SPAC2F7.03c' (pom1).

tools.name: PomBase_get_go_annotations
tools.summary: Returns GO annotations by aspect for an S. pombe gene from PomBase.
tools.description: Get Gene Ontology annotations (biological_process / molecular_function / cellular_component) for a fission-yeast (S. pombe) gene from PomBase, with per-aspect counts and resolved term names. Example: SPBC11B10.09 (cdc2) returns BP terms like GO:0000082 'G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle', plus MF and CC terms.

gene_id.description: PomBase systematic ID. Examples: 'SPBC11B10.09' (cdc2).

tools.name: PomBase_get_interactions
tools.summary: Returns physical and genetic interactions with evidence for an S. pombe gene.
tools.description: Get physical and genetic interactions for a fission-yeast (S. pombe) gene from PomBase, each with evidence method, reference (PMID), throughput, and source database. Example: SPBC11B10.09 (cdc2) has ~100 physical interactions (e.g. SPAC1006.03c/red1 via Affinity Capture-MS, PMID:24713849, BIOGRID) and ~118 genetic interactions.

gene_id.description: PomBase systematic ID. Examples: 'SPBC11B10.09' (cdc2).

tools.name: PomBase_get_orthologs
tools.summary: Returns human and budding yeast orthologs of an S. pombe gene.
tools.description: Get human and S. cerevisiae orthologs of a fission-yeast (S. pombe) gene from PomBase. Returns ortholog IDs with taxon (9606=human via HGNC, 4932=budding yeast via systematic name). Example: SPBC11B10.09 (cdc2) returns human CDKs HGNC:1722/1771/1772 (taxon 9606) and S. cerevisiae CDC28 / YBR160W (taxon 4932).

gene_id.description: PomBase systematic ID. Examples: 'SPBC11B10.09' (cdc2), 'SPAC1006.03c' (red1).

tools.name: PomBase_search_genes
tools.summary: Searches PomBase S. pombe genes by name, systematic ID or product.
tools.description: Search PomBase for fission yeast (S. pombe) genes by name, systematic ID, or protein product keyword. Searches across 12,600+ gene entries. Returns matching genes with systematic IDs, gene names, and protein products. Example: searching 'kinase' returns CDK and other kinase genes; searching 'cdc' returns cell division cycle genes.

query.description: Search query - gene name, systematic ID prefix, or product keyword. Examples: 'cdc2', 'kinase', 'SPAC', 'pom1'.

limit.description: Maximum results to return (1-50, default 10).

tools.name: PopGen_fst
tools.summary: Calculates Weir-Cockerham Fst between two populations from allele frequencies and sample sizes.
tools.description: Calculate the Weir-Cockerham (1984) theta Fst estimator between two populations given allele frequencies and sample sizes, including the n_c sample-size correction (theta = (MSP - MSG) / (MSP + (n_c - 1) * MSG)) so the result reflects allele-frequency divergence rather than sample size. Fst quantifies genetic differentiation: <0.05 little, 0.05-0.15 moderate, 0.15-0.25 great, >0.25 very great differentiation. Useful for measuring population structure and divergence at individual loci.

n1.description: Sample size (number of individuals) for population 1

n2.description: Sample size (number of individuals) for population 2

tools.name: PopGen_haplotype_count
tools.summary: Estimates distinct haplotypes after recombination over generations for a multi-SNP region.
tools.description: Estimate distinct haplotypes after recombination across generations for a region with multiple biallelic SNPs. Reports maximum theoretical haplotypes (2^n), expected crossovers per gamete, probability of at least one recombination event, and estimated haplotype diversity based on LD decay. Useful for understanding recombination impact on genetic variation.

n_snps.description: Number of biallelic SNP loci in the region

generations.description: Number of generations of random mating (default 1)

tools.name: PopGen_hwe_test
tools.summary: Tests Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium from observed genotype counts with chi-square.
tools.description: Test Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a biallelic locus given observed genotype counts (AA, Aa, aa). Computes allele frequencies, expected genotype counts under HWE, chi-square statistic with 1 df, and p-value. Reports whether the locus is in HWE (p > 0.05) and, if not, whether heterozygote excess or deficit is observed. Useful for detecting selection, inbreeding, assortative mating, or genotyping error at individual loci.

obs_AA.description: Observed count of homozygous dominant (AA) genotypes

obs_aa.description: Observed count of homozygous recessive (aa) genotypes

tools.name: PopGen_inbreeding
tools.summary: Computes inbreeding coefficient F for a pedigree type over generations.
tools.description: Compute inbreeding coefficient F for a known pedigree type over one or more generations. Supports: self, full-sib, half-sib, first-cousin, double-first-cousin, uncle-niece, aunt-nephew, half-first-cousin, second-cousin. Uses the recurrence F_t = base_F + (1-base_F)*F_{t-1} for iterated inbreeding. Reports F per generation, cumulative F, and retained heterozygosity.

tools.name: Progenetix_cnv_search
tools.summary: Searches cancer biosamples with CNVs (gains/losses) in a genomic region and disease filter.
tools.description: Search for cancer biosamples with copy number variations (CNVs) in a specific genomic region. Combines disease filter with genomic coordinates to find samples with amplifications or deletions in genes of interest. Uses RefSeq chromosome accessions for coordinates. Example: searching for EGFR amplifications (refseq:NC_000007.14:55019017-55211628, DUP) in breast cancer (NCIT:C4017) returns 9 matching biosamples.

start.description: Start position (1-based, GRCh38). Example: 55019017 for EGFR start.

end.description: End position (1-based, GRCh38). Example: 55211628 for EGFR end.

variant_type.description: CNV type: 'DUP' for amplification/duplication, 'DEL' for deletion. Leave empty for any CNV type.

filters.description: Optional NCIt ontology code to filter by cancer type. Example: 'NCIT:C4017' for breast cancer.

limit.description: Maximum number of biosamples to return (default: 10).

tools.name: Progenetix_get_cnv_frequencies
tools.summary: Returns genome-wide gain and loss frequencies per cytoband for a cancer type from Progenetix.
tools.description: Get the genome-wide aggregate CNV frequency profile for a cancer type from Progenetix — the signature Progenetix output. For each genomic interval bin (cytoband), returns the gain frequency and loss frequency aggregated across all samples of a Progenetix collation, selected by NCIt code. Example: NCIT:C4017 (Breast Ductal Carcinoma) returns sampleCount 13869 across 3106 interval bins; NCIT:C3058 (Glioblastoma) bin 1p36.33 has gain_frequency 4.258 and loss_frequency 5.278.

filters.description: NCIt ontology code identifying the cancer-type collation. Examples: 'NCIT:C4017' (Breast Ductal Carcinoma), 'NCIT:C3058' (Glioblastoma), 'NCIT:C9145' (AML), 'NCIT:C3224' (Melanoma), 'NCIT:C4872' (Lung Adenocarcinoma).

max_intervals.description: Optional cap on the number of interval bins returned (default: all ~3000 bins).

tools.name: Progenetix_list_cohorts
tools.summary: Lists Progenetix cancer CNV cohorts (e.g. TCGA) with IDs, sizes and data types.
tools.description: List available cohorts in the Progenetix cancer CNV database. Returns cohort IDs, names, sizes, and data types. Progenetix organizes samples into cohorts like TCGA, DIPG studies, and curated cancer sets. Example: returns 6 cohorts including TCGA (517 samples) and DIPG (16 samples).

limit.description: Maximum number of cohorts to return (default: 10).

tools.name: Progenetix_search_biosamples
tools.summary: Searches Progenetix tumor biosamples by NCIt disease code, returning IDs, histology and stage.
tools.description: Search cancer tumor biosamples in the Progenetix database by NCIt disease ontology code. Progenetix contains genome-wide copy number variation (CNV) profiles from over 100,000 tumor samples. Returns biosample IDs, histological diagnosis, pathological stage, and external references. Uses the GA4GH Beacon v2 protocol. Example: NCIT:C3058 returns 28 glioblastoma biosamples with histological classification and study references.

filters.description: NCIt ontology code to filter biosamples by cancer type. Examples: 'NCIT:C3058' (Glioblastoma), 'NCIT:C4017' (Breast Carcinoma), 'NCIT:C9145' (Acute Myeloid Leukemia), 'NCIT:C3224' (Melanoma), 'NCIT:C4872' (Lung Adenocarcinoma), 'NCIT:C3167' (Neuroblastoma).

limit.description: Maximum number of biosamples to return (default: 10).

skip.description: Number of results to skip for pagination (default: 0).

tools.name: ProtVar_get_function
tools.summary: Returns UniProt functional features and structural context at an amino-acid position, optionally for a variant residue.
tools.description: Get functional annotations at a specific amino acid position from ProtVar. Returns annotated UniProt features overlapping that position (domains, active sites, binding sites, PTMs), the protein's function description, and structural context. Use to understand the biological importance of a variant site before interpreting pathogenicity scores. Example: P04637 position 175 returns DNA-binding domain overlap and TP53 tumor suppressor function.

position.description: Amino acid position in the protein (1-based).

variant_aa.description: Single-letter code for the variant amino acid (e.g. 'H' for histidine). Optional but recommended.

tools.name: ProtVar_get_population
tools.summary: Returns co-located variants with gnomAD/1000G frequencies, ClinVar significance and SIFT/PolyPhen at a protein position.
tools.description: Get population observation data for a protein variant position from ProtVar. Returns co-located variants with population allele frequencies (gnomAD, 1000Genomes), clinical significance (ClinVar), and computational predictions (SIFT, PolyPhen).

position.description: Amino acid position in the protein (1-based).

genomic_location.description: Genomic coordinate (GRCh38) for the variant. Obtain from ProtVar_map_variant output.

tools.name: ProtVar_map_variant
tools.summary: Maps a protein change, rsID or VCF-style variant to genomic coordinates with AlphaMissense, EVE and ESM scores.
tools.description: Map a human protein variant to genomic coordinates and get pathogenicity predictions (AlphaMissense, EVE, ESM, conservation). Accepts three input formats: (1) protein 'ACCESSION CHANGE' e.g. 'P04637 R175H'; (2) dbSNP rsID e.g. 'rs1799966'; (3) VCF-style genomic 'chr17 43057065 . T G'. Returns isoform mappings, consequence type, and variant effect scores.

variant.description: Variant identifier in one of three formats: (1) 'UniProtAccession SingleLetterChange' e.g. 'P04637 R175H' (TP53 R175H); (2) dbSNP rsID e.g. 'rs1799966'; (3) VCF genomic 'chr17 43057065 . REF ALT'. Note: colon-separated 'chr:pos:ref:alt' is auto-converted to VCF format.

tools.name: QuickGO_annotations_by_gene
tools.summary: Returns GO annotations with evidence codes for a gene product from QuickGO.
tools.description: Search Gene Ontology (GO) annotations for a specific gene product using the EBI QuickGO browser. Returns GO terms annotated to the protein/gene with evidence codes, qualifiers, and annotation sources. Accepts UniProtKB accessions (e.g., 'UniProtKB:P04637' for TP53). Provides more detailed annotation data than the standard GO API, including evidence provenance and assigned-by information. Useful for understanding gene function, localization, and biological processes.

gene_product_id.description: Gene product identifier, typically a UniProtKB accession. Format: 'UniProtKB:P04637' (TP53), 'UniProtKB:P38398' (BRCA1), 'UniProtKB:P00533' (EGFR).

aspect.description: Filter by GO aspect: 'biological_process', 'molecular_function', or 'cellular_component'. Default: all aspects.

taxon_id.description: Filter by NCBI taxonomy ID. Example: 9606 (human), 10090 (mouse).

limit.description: Maximum number of annotations to return. Default: 25, max: 100.

tools.name: QuickGO_annotations_by_goterm
tools.summary: Lists gene products annotated to a GO term with evidence, optionally by taxon.
tools.description: Search for all gene products annotated with a specific Gene Ontology (GO) term using the EBI QuickGO browser. Returns the proteins/genes associated with the GO term, their evidence codes, and annotation sources. Can be filtered by species (taxon_id). Useful for finding all genes involved in a biological process, molecular function, or cellular component. Example: GO:0006915 (apoptotic process) returns 6800+ human annotations.

go_id.description: Gene Ontology term accession. Examples: 'GO:0006915' (apoptotic process), 'GO:0008150' (biological process), 'GO:0005634' (nucleus), 'GO:0003677' (DNA binding).

taxon_id.description: Filter by NCBI taxonomy ID. Example: 9606 (human), 10090 (mouse), 7227 (fly).

limit.description: Maximum number of annotations to return. Default: 25, max: 100.

tools.name: REBASE_get_enzyme
tools.summary: Returns REBASE restriction enzyme recognition site, cut position, ends, methylation sensitivity and suppliers.
tools.description: Look up a restriction enzyme in REBASE, the reference catalogue of ~6,000 enzymes from New England Biolabs. Returns the recognition sequence with its cut point, whether the cut leaves blunt or sticky ends, the source organism, methylation sensitivity, commercial availability, and isoschizomers. Example: name='EcoRI' returns G^AATTC. The DNA_find_restriction_sites and DNA_virtual_digest calculators work from 25 curated enzymes; use this to look up anything outside that set.

tools.name: REBASE_list_isoschizomers
tools.summary: Lists restriction enzymes sharing a recognition specificity with the named enzyme, commercial first.
tools.description: List every restriction enzyme sharing a prototype with the named enzyme, i.e. all enzymes with the same recognition specificity. Commercially available enzymes are listed first, so this answers 'which enzyme can I actually buy that cuts like this one'. Example: name='EcoRI'.

name.description: Enzyme name to find isoschizomers of, e.g. 'EcoRI'.

tools.name: REBASE_search_by_site
tools.summary: Finds restriction enzymes recognizing a site or cutting a given DNA sequence, with cut counts.
tools.description: Find restriction enzymes by what they recognize. Give site to find every enzyme reading an exact recognition sequence (site='GAATTC'), or give sequence to find every enzyme that would cut a DNA sequence, with the number of cut sites each produces. IUPAC ambiguity codes in enzyme sites are expanded, so degenerate recognition sequences match correctly. Set only_commercial=true to restrict to enzymes you can buy.

site.description: Exact recognition sequence to match, e.g. 'GAATTC'. Mutually exclusive with sequence.

sequence.description: DNA sequence to find cutters for, e.g. a plasmid region. Mutually exclusive with site.

only_commercial.description: If true, return only commercially available enzymes.

limit.description: Maximum enzymes to return (default 25, max 200).

tools.name: RGD_get_annotations
tools.summary: Returns RGD disease, phenotype, pathway and GO annotations for a rat gene.
tools.description: Get disease, phenotype, pathway, and GO annotations for a rat gene from RGD. Returns curated annotations with ontology terms, evidence codes, and qualifiers. Filter by aspect: D=Disease, P=Pathway, W=Phenotype, F=Molecular Function, C=Cellular Component, E=Expression. Essential for rat disease model research and toxicogenomics.

aspect.description: Filter by annotation type: 'D' (Disease), 'P' (Pathway), 'W' (Phenotype), 'F' (Function), 'C' (Component), 'E' (Expression). Leave empty for all.

tools.name: RGD_get_gene
tools.summary: Returns RGD rat gene symbol, name, description, type and Ensembl cross-reference.
tools.description: Get detailed rat gene information from the Rat Genome Database by RGD ID. Returns gene symbol, name, description (including AGR-aggregated functional summary with disease associations, pathways, and interactions), gene type, and Ensembl cross-reference. Use when looking up specific rat genes for toxicology, pharmacology, or disease model research.

rgd_id.description: RGD gene ID (numeric, e.g., '2218' for Brca1). Can include 'RGD:' prefix.

tools.name: RGD_get_orthologs
tools.summary: Returns orthologs of a rat gene across species from RGD.
tools.description: Get orthologs of a rat gene across species (human, mouse, chinchilla, dog, pig, etc.) from RGD. Returns ortholog gene symbols, RGD IDs, names, and species. Use for cross-species comparison in model organism genetics, finding human disease gene orthologs in rat.

tools.name: RGD_get_qtls_in_region
tools.summary: Returns RGD QTLs overlapping a genomic region with LOD score and p-value.
tools.description: Get QTLs (Quantitative Trait Loci) overlapping a genomic region from the Rat Genome Database (RGD's flagship data type). Returns QTL symbol, name, RGD ID, LOD score, p-value, and inheritance type. Requires a chromosome, start/stop coordinates, and a map_key identifying the assembly (e.g., 360 for rat rn7/GRCr8, 38 for human GRCh38, 35 for mouse GRCm39). Example: chromosome='10', start=1, stop=50000000, map_key=360 returns QTL Uae41 'Urinary albumin excretion QTL 41' lod=5.26 rgdId=7387235.

map_key.description: Assembly map key. 360=rat rn7/GRCr8, 372=rat mRatBN7.2, 38=human GRCh38, 17=human GRCh37, 35=mouse GRCm39, 18=mouse GRCm38.

tools.name: RGD_get_strain
tools.summary: Returns an RGD rat strain record with type, genetics, origin and background.
tools.description: Get the full Rat Genome Database (RGD) record for a single rat strain by its exact strain symbol (e.g. 'SHR', 'BN', 'SS', 'WKY', 'GK'). Returns the strain RGD ID, name, full strain name, substrain, strain type, genetics formula, origin, background strain, and description. Use RGD_search_strains first if you only know a keyword.

symbol.description: Exact rat strain symbol (case-insensitive), e.g. 'SHR' (spontaneously hypertensive rat), 'BN' (Brown Norway), 'SS' (Dahl salt-sensitive).

tools.name: RGD_get_strain_annotations
tools.summary: Returns curated disease, phenotype and variant-trait annotations for an RGD rat strain.
tools.description: Get curated disease, phenotype, and variant-trait ontology annotations for a rat strain from the Rat Genome Database (RGD), by strain symbol (e.g. 'SHR', 'BN', 'SS'). This exposes RGD's rat disease-MODEL annotations - for example SHR is annotated to 'Left Ventricular Hypertrophy' (disease, MODEL: spontaneous) and 'arterial blood pressure trait' (phenotype). Each annotation includes the ontology term, accession (DOID/VT/CMO/MP/RS), category, qualifier, and evidence code. Optional 'category' filter: disease, phenotype, strain, pathway, biological_process, molecular_function, cellular_component.

category.description: Optional annotation category filter: 'disease', 'phenotype', 'strain', 'pathway', etc. Omit to return all categories.

tools.name: RGD_resolve_symbol_or_region
tools.summary: Resolves a rat gene symbol to its RGD record or lists genes overlapping a genomic region.
tools.description: Resolve a rat gene symbol to its native RGD record/ID, or list genes overlapping a genomic region. Symbol mode: provide 'symbol' (and optional species_type_key, default 3=rat) -> returns RGD key, rgd_id, name, type. Region mode: provide chromosome + start + stop + map_key -> returns genes in that interval. Example: symbol='Tp53' returns key=1887 rgd_id=3889 name='tumor protein p53'; region chromosome='10', start=1, stop=5000000, map_key=360 returns Mir484 rgdId=2325341.

symbol.description: Rat gene symbol, e.g. 'Tp53'. Use this for symbol mode.

species_type_key.description: Species type key for symbol mode (default 3=rat, 1=human, 2=mouse).

map_key.description: Assembly map key for region mode (e.g. 360 for rat rn7).

tools.name: RGD_search_genes
tools.summary: Searches RGD genes by symbol or keyword for rat, human or mouse.
tools.description: Search for rat genes by symbol or keyword in the Rat Genome Database. Returns matching genes with RGD IDs, symbols, names, types, and descriptions. Supports rat, human, and mouse species. Use for finding rat orthologs, toxicology studies, or rat disease model genes.

query.description: Gene symbol or keyword (e.g., 'Brca1', 'Tp53', 'insulin')

species.description: Species to search: 'rat' (default), 'human', 'mouse'

tools.name: RGD_search_strains
tools.summary: Searches the RGD rat strain catalog by keyword and strain type.
tools.description: Search the Rat Genome Database (RGD) rat strain catalog by keyword and/or strain type. Rat inbred/congenic/transgenic strains are RGD's flagship rat-specific resource (not in Alliance of Genome Resources or MGI). Provide 'query' (a keyword matched against symbol, name, full strain name, genetics, and description) and/or 'strain_type' (one of: inbred, congenic, mutant, transgenic, recombinant_inbred, outbred, consomic, coisogenic, segregating_inbred, hybrid, wild, conplastic, advanced_intercross_line, transchromosomal). At least one of the two must be supplied. Returns matching strains with their RGD ID, symbol, name, type, genetics, and origin.

query.description: Keyword to match against strain symbol, name, genetics, and description (case-insensitive substring). Example: 'hypertensive' or 'Dahl'.

limit.description: Maximum number of strains to return (default 25, max 200).

tools.name: RNAcentral_get_by_accession
tools.summary: Returns an RNAcentral ncRNA entry with annotations and source cross-references.
tools.description: Retrieve a single RNAcentral entry by accession for detailed annotations and source cross-references. Use for cross-database ID mapping and metadata.

tools.name: RNAcentral_get_genome_locations
tools.summary: Returns chromosome, strand and coordinates of an RNAcentral ncRNA in a species.
tools.description: Get the genomic coordinates of a non-coding RNA in a specific organism from RNAcentral. Provide an RNAcentral URS identifier (e.g. 'URS00003B7674' for let-7a) and an NCBI taxonomy id (e.g. 9606 for human). Returns each genomic mapping: chromosome, strand, start, end, UCSC/Ensembl assembly (GRCh38), and GCA accession. RNAcentral aggregates ncRNAs (miRNA, lncRNA, rRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, etc.) from 40+ member databases.

urs_id.description: RNAcentral URS identifier, e.g. 'URS00003B7674'. A trailing '_taxid' suffix is accepted and stripped.

taxid.description: NCBI taxonomy id of the organism whose genome mapping is requested, e.g. 9606 (human), 10090 (mouse). Required.

tools.name: RNAcentral_get_region_ncRNAs
tools.summary: Lists RNAcentral non-coding RNAs overlapping a genomic region for a species.
tools.description: List all RNAcentral non-coding RNAs overlapping a genome locus, aggregated from 50+ member databases (miRBase, snoRNA, tRNA, lncRNA, piRNA, etc.). Provide a species (default 'homo_sapiens') and either a 'region' string ('2:39745816-39826679') or discrete 'chromosome'/'start'/'end'. Returns overlapping ncRNA transcripts and their exon features with biotype, strand and coordinates, split into data.transcripts and data.exons. Use to annotate what ncRNAs sit in a region of interest. Public, no authentication.

region.description: Locus as 'chr:start-end' (1-based), e.g. '2:39745816-39826679'. Omit if giving chromosome/start/end.

species.description: Ensembl species slug (default 'homo_sapiens'). E.g. 'mus_musculus', 'danio_rerio'.

chromosome.description: Chromosome name without 'chr' prefix, e.g. '2'. Used with start/end when 'region' is omitted.

start.description: Region start (1-based). Used with chromosome/end when 'region' is omitted.

end.description: Region end (1-based). Used with chromosome/start when 'region' is omitted.

tools.name: RNAcentral_get_sequence
tools.summary: Returns the FASTA nucleotide sequence of an RNAcentral ncRNA.
tools.description: Get the nucleotide sequence (FASTA) of a non-coding RNA from RNAcentral. Provide an RNAcentral URS identifier (e.g. 'URS00003B7674'). Returns the FASTA header, the full RNA sequence string, and its length.

urs_id.description: RNAcentral URS identifier, e.g. 'URS00003B7674'. A trailing '_taxid' suffix is accepted and stripped.

tools.name: RNAcentral_get_xrefs_and_pubs
tools.summary: Returns per-source cross-references (NCBI gene, Ensembl/GENCODE transcripts) and publications for an RNAcentral entry.
tools.description: Get the resolved per-source cross-references AND literature for an RNAcentral entry in one call. Returns the full xref list (with database name, taxid, accession id, NCBI gene id, miRBase mature/precursor products, Ensembl/GENCODE transcript ids, RefSeq, etc.) under data.xrefs, and the publications list (title, authors, PMID, DOI) under data.publications. Use after RNAcentral_search or RNAcentral_get_by_accession to map an URS id to external databases and supporting papers. Example: URS000063A371 returns 8 xrefs (database=Rfam, taxid=7955, accession id 'CR381647.10:84955..85035:rfam') and 8 publications (e.g. PMID 12844358, DOI 10.1186/gb-2003-4-7-r42).

tools.name: RNAcentral_search
tools.summary: Searches RNAcentral ncRNA records (miRNA, lncRNA, rRNA) by query.
tools.description: Search aggregated ncRNA records (miRNA, rRNA, lncRNA, etc.) across sources via RNAcentral. Use to find accessions, types, species, and descriptions for ncRNA analysis.

query.description: Keyword, accession, or sequence-based query (per RNAcentral API).

page_size.description: Number of records per page (1–100).

tools.name: RNAseq_edger_limma_de
tools.summary: Runs edgeR QL-F or limma-voom differential expression on a count matrix and metadata.
tools.description: Bulk RNA-seq differential expression via edgeR (QL-F) or limma-voom on a count matrix + sample metadata — the two standard DE frameworks alongside DESeq2 (run_deseq2_analysis). method='edger' (good for small replicate counts) or 'limma' (large n / complex designs). Returns DEG counts at FDR-only, FDR+|logFC|, and strict (FDR+|logFC|+expression) filters, optional per-gene logFC/FDR, and the full ranked table on disk. Requires Rscript with Bioconductor edgeR + limma.

counts_file.description: Path to counts CSV (genes x samples; first column = gene IDs)

metadata_file.description: Path to sample metadata CSV (one row per sample)

design.description: Design formula, e.g. '~ condition' or '~ batch + condition' (default '~ condition')

lfc_threshold.description: abs(logFC) threshold for the sig sets (default 0.5)

expr_threshold.description: Expression threshold (logCPM/AveExpr) for the strict set (default 0)

exclude_samples.description: Comma-separated sample IDs to drop before analysis

report_genes.description: Comma-separated gene IDs to report individual logFC/FDR for

tools.name: ReMap_get_peaks_in_region
tools.summary: Returns ReMap ChIP-seq transcriptional regulator peaks overlapping a genomic interval.
tools.description: Retrieve all ChIP-seq transcriptional-regulator (TR) binding peaks from the ReMap catalog that overlap a genomic interval. Give a region (chrom:start-end) and get back every overlapping peak with its genomic coordinates plus the bound TF, the cell line/tissue (biotype), the source experiment accession (GEO/ENCODE), and any treatments. This is the defining ReMap capability (region in -> all overlapping TR peaks out). Use for: enumerating which transcription factors bind a locus, finding regulatory occupancy of a promoter/enhancer interval, listing TFs near a variant. Keep regions modest (<=1 Mb) - large intervals can return tens of thousands of peaks.

region.description: Genomic interval as chrom:start-end (e.g. 'chr1:1000000-1100000'). Commas in coordinates are tolerated.

datatype.description: Peak datatype: 'all' for the non-redundant merged peak set across all TFs.

limit.description: Optional cap on the number of peaks returned (peak_count still reports the true total). Omit to return all overlapping peaks.

tools.name: ReMap_get_transcription_factor_binding
tools.summary: Returns ReMap transcription factor binding sites for a gene and cell type.
tools.description: Get transcription factor binding sites from ReMap database for specific genes and cell types

gene_name.description: Gene symbol (e.g., BRCA1, TP53, MYC)

limit.description: Number of results to return

tools.name: ReMap_list_datasets_for_target
tools.summary: Lists ReMap ChIP-seq datasets for a transcription factor with optional peak counts.
tools.description: List ReMap ChIP-seq datasets for a transcription factor, one row per dataset, optionally filtered to a GEO/ENCODE experiment accession and optionally with each dataset's peak count. A GEO series is NOT one dataset: GSE23852 for FOXA1 holds two (MCF-7_ETOH and MCF-7_E2) with different peak counts, so 'how many peaks in experiment X' usually needs the per-dataset split rather than a single number. Set count_peaks=true to download each dataset's BED and count peaks (slower).

experiment.description: Optional experiment accession prefix to filter on, e.g. 'GSE23852'. Dataset names look like 'GSE23852.FOXA1.MCF-7_ETOH'.

count_peaks.description: Download each dataset's BED and report its peak count. Slower; use when the question asks how many peaks.

tools.name: ReactomeAnalysis_expression_analysis
tools.summary: Runs Reactome expression analysis mapping fold-change values for identifiers onto pathways.
tools.description: Quantitative EXPRESSION analysis: map fold-change or numeric expression values onto Reactome pathways (analysis type=EXPRESSION). Unlike ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_enrichment (which only accepts a plain newline-separated identifier list and runs overrepresentation), this tool submits TAB-DELIMITED 'GENE\tVALUE' rows so Reactome treats the input as an expression matrix and overlays each value per pathway. Each returned pathway carries 'entities_exp' (the matched expression values for that pathway) and the result reports the expression column names plus the min/max of the submitted values. Example: submitting 'PTEN\t2.5\nTP53\t-1.8\nEGFR\t3.1' returns analysis_type=EXPRESSION with pathways such as 'Regulation of TP53 Expression' carrying entities_exp=[-1.8]. INTERPRETING RESULTS: rank pathways by 'fdr' or 'p_value' - those are the enrichment statistics. 'entities_coverage' (= entities_found / entities_total) is the fraction of a pathway your identifiers cover. 'pathway_size_fraction_of_reactome' (deprecated alias 'entities_ratio') is Reactome's raw 'ratio': pathway size over Reactome's entity universe for the species, independent of the identifiers you submit - never rank by it.

identifiers.description: Tab-delimited expression rows, one identifier per line as 'GENE<TAB>VALUE'. Newline-separated rows. Gene symbols, UniProt, or Ensembl IDs in the first column; numeric fold-change/expression value(s) in following tab-separated column(s). Example: 'PTEN\t2.5\nTP53\t-1.8\nEGFR\t3.1'.

page_size.description: Number of pathways to return (default 20, max 50).

include_disease.description: Include disease pathways in results (default true).

projection.description: Project identifiers to human pathways via orthology (default false; set true for non-human input).

tools.name: ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_enrichment
tools.summary: Runs Reactome overrepresentation analysis on gene symbols, UniProt or Ensembl IDs.
tools.description: Perform pathway overrepresentation (enrichment) analysis using the Reactome Analysis Service. Submit a list of gene symbols, UniProt IDs, or Ensembl IDs and identify which Reactome pathways are statistically enriched. Returns pathways ranked by p-value with FDR (False Discovery Rate) correction, entity counts, and reaction coverage. Supports projection to human pathways for cross-species analysis. INTERPRETING RESULTS: rank pathways by 'fdr' or 'p_value' - those are the enrichment statistics. 'entities_coverage' (= entities_found / entities_total) is the fraction of a pathway your identifiers cover. 'pathway_size_fraction_of_reactome' (deprecated alias 'entities_ratio') is Reactome's raw 'ratio': pathway size over Reactome's entity universe for the species, independent of the identifiers you submit - never rank by it. Example: submitting TP53, BRCA1, CDH1, EGFR, KRAS returns 394 enriched pathways including 'Developmental Lineage of Mammary Gland Myoepithelial Cells' (p=3.94e-08) and 'Signaling by ERBB2 KD Mutants'.

identifiers.description:
Newline-separated list of gene/protein identifiers. Supports gene symbols (TP53, BRCA1), UniProt IDs (P04637, P38398), or Ensembl IDs. Example: 'TP53
BRCA1
CDH1
EGFR
KRAS'.

page_size.description: Number of pathways to return (default 20, max 50).

include_disease.description: Include disease pathways in results (default true).

projection.description: Project identifiers to human Reactome pathways for cross-species analysis (default true).

tools.name: ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_found_entities
tools.summary: Lists submitted identifiers matching a hit pathway in a Reactome analysis, with cross-references.
tools.description: Per-pathway found-entities drill-down: for an analysis token and a specific HIT pathway, list exactly which submitted identifiers matched that pathway and their Reactome cross-references (UniProt/ENSEMBL ids each input mapsTo). Standard token result tools return only the pathway summary table - they never reveal WHICH of your genes landed in a given pathway. Obtain the token from ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_enrichment / _expression_analysis (data.token), then pass that token plus a pathway stable id. Example: token from submitting PTEN,TP53,EGFR,BRCA1 with pathway 'R-HSA-3700989' returns identifiers including {id:'BRCA1', mapsTo:[{resource:'UNIPROT', ids:['P38398']},{resource:'ENSEMBL', ids:['ENST00000357654','ENSG00000012048']}]}.

token.description: Analysis token from a previous ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_enrichment or ReactomeAnalysis_expression_analysis call (the 'token' field in its data). Tokens expire after a period, so run the analysis first.

pathway.description: Reactome pathway stable id of a hit pathway from the analysis result (e.g. 'R-HSA-3700989').

resource.description: Resource to map entities against (default 'TOTAL'). Other options: 'UNIPROT', 'ENSEMBL'.

tools.name: ReactomeAnalysis_species_comparison
tools.summary: Projects gene/protein identifiers from another species onto human Reactome pathways for enrichment.
tools.description: Perform Reactome pathway analysis with cross-species projection. Submit protein/gene identifiers from any supported species and Reactome will project them to human pathways, enabling comparison of pathway enrichment across species. This uses the same overrepresentation analysis but ensures identifiers are mapped via orthology to human pathways. Example: submitting mouse protein IDs returns enriched human Reactome pathways with mapping statistics. INTERPRETING RESULTS: rank pathways by 'fdr' or 'p_value' - those are the enrichment statistics. 'entities_coverage' (= entities_found / entities_total) is the fraction of a pathway your identifiers cover. 'pathway_size_fraction_of_reactome' (deprecated alias 'entities_ratio') is Reactome's raw 'ratio': pathway size over Reactome's entity universe for the species, independent of the identifiers you submit - never rank by it.

identifiers.description: Newline-separated list of gene/protein identifiers from any species. Supports UniProt, Ensembl, or gene symbols. Example: 'Trp53\nBrca1\nCdh1' (mouse gene symbols).

species.description: NCBI taxonomy ID of the source species (default 9606 for human). Examples: 10090 (mouse), 7955 (zebrafish), 7227 (fly).

page_size.description: Number of pathways to return (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: ReactomeAnalysis_token_result
tools.summary: Retrieves previously computed Reactome analysis results by token with pagination.
tools.description: Retrieve previously computed Reactome pathway analysis results using an analysis token. Tokens are returned from pathway_enrichment or species_comparison analyses and can be used to access results without rerunning the analysis. Useful for paginating through large result sets or sharing analysis results. The token contains the full analysis result and is valid for a limited time. INTERPRETING RESULTS: rank pathways by 'fdr' or 'p_value' - those are the enrichment statistics. 'entities_coverage' (= entities_found / entities_total) is the fraction of a pathway your identifiers cover. 'pathway_size_fraction_of_reactome' (deprecated alias 'entities_ratio') is Reactome's raw 'ratio': pathway size over Reactome's entity universe for the species, independent of the identifiers you submit - never rank by it.

token.description: Analysis token from a previous ReactomeAnalysis_pathway_enrichment or ReactomeAnalysis_species_comparison call.

page_size.description: Number of pathways per page (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: ReactomeInteractors_get_entity_pathways
tools.summary: Returns Reactome pathways containing a given entity stable ID, flagging disease pathways.
tools.description: Find Reactome biological pathways that contain a specific molecular entity. Returns pathway stable IDs, names, and whether they are disease-associated. Use Reactome stable IDs (e.g., R-HSA-199420 for PTEN) obtained from ReactomeInteractors_search_entity. Example: R-HSA-199420 (PTEN) participates in 10 pathways including PI3K/AKT signaling, PTEN regulation, and TCR signaling.

entity_id.description: Reactome stable identifier for the entity. Use ReactomeInteractors_search_entity to find IDs. Examples: 'R-HSA-199420' (PTEN), 'R-HSA-69541' (TP53 tetramer), 'R-HSA-8869337' (TP53).

species.description: NCBI taxonomy ID for species filter (default: 9606 for human). Examples: 9606 (human), 10090 (mouse).

tools.name: Reactome_get_participant_reference_entities
tools.summary: Returns reference entities (UniProt proteins, ChEBI chemicals) for participants of a Reactome event.
tools.description: Get reference entities for participants of a reaction or event. Returns list of reference entities (UniProt proteins, ChEBI chemicals, etc.) associated with the participants, including database identifiers and names.

stId.description: Event Stable ID (reaction or pathway, e.g., 'R-HSA-111289'). To find reaction IDs, use Reactome_get_pathway_reactions with a pathway ID. To find pathway IDs, use Reactome_list_top_pathways.

tools.name: Reactome_get_participants
tools.summary: Returns physical entities (proteins, complexes, small molecules) participating in a Reactome event.
tools.description: Get all participants (physical entities) of a reaction or event. Returns list of physical entities (proteins, complexes, small molecules) participating in the event, including their reference entities.

stId.description: Event Stable ID (reaction or pathway, e.g., 'R-HSA-111289'). To find reaction IDs, use Reactome_get_pathway_reactions with a pathway ID. To find pathway IDs, use Reactome_list_top_pathways.

tools.name: Reactome_get_pathways_low_entity
tools.summary: Returns the most specific Reactome pathways containing a given entity.
tools.description: Get low-level pathways (most specific pathways) containing a specific entity. Returns pathways at the lowest level of the hierarchy.

id.description: Entity Stable ID (pathway, reaction, or physical entity, e.g., 'R-HSA-73817'). To find pathway IDs, use Reactome_list_top_pathways. To find reaction IDs, use Reactome_get_pathway_reactions. To find entity IDs, use Reactome_get_participants.

tools.name: Reactome_map_uniprot_to_pathways
tools.summary: Maps a UniProt accession to all Reactome pathways containing it.
tools.description: Map a UniProt protein identifier to Reactome pathways. Returns all pathways that contain this protein.

uniprot_id.description: UniProt protein accession (e.g., 'P04637' for TP53, 'P00533' for EGFR)

tools.name: Reactome_map_uniprot_to_reactions
tools.summary: Maps a UniProt accession to Reactome reactions involving it.
tools.description: Map a UniProt protein identifier to Reactome reactions. Returns all reactions that involve this protein.

uniprot_id.description: UniProt protein accession (e.g., 'P04637' for TP53, 'P00533' for EGFR)

tools.name: RegulomeDB_query_variant
tools.summary: Returns RegulomeDB regulatory evidence and score for a variant by rsID.
tools.description: Query RegulomeDB for regulatory variant annotations using rsID

variant.description: Alias for rsid. dbSNP rsID (e.g., 'rs7903146', 'rs429358').

tools.name: Rfam_accession_to_id
tools.summary: Converts an Rfam accession to its family ID/name.
tools.description: Convert Rfam accession to family ID/name. Takes RF accession (e.g., RF00360) and returns human-readable family name (e.g., snoZ107_R87). Simple ID conversion utility. Use for: displaying readable names, documentation, cross-referencing, data integration. Quick lookup with plain text response.

tools.name: Rfam_get_alignment
tools.summary: Returns the Rfam seed multiple sequence alignment in Stockholm, Pfam or FASTA format.
tools.description: Get RNA family seed alignment in multiple formats. Returns curated multiple sequence alignment used to build covariance model. Formats: stockholm (default, with structure annotation), pfam (stockholm single-line), fasta (gapped), fastau (ungapped). Optional gzip compression for large alignments. Use for: sequence analysis, structure prediction, phylogenetic studies, homology detection. Alignments show conserved positions and base pairing.

family_id.description: Required: Rfam accession or family name

format.description: Alignment format: stockholm (structured), pfam (single-line), fasta (gapped), fastau (ungapped)

tools.name: Rfam_get_covariance_model
tools.summary: Returns the Infernal covariance model for an Rfam family.
tools.description: Get Infernal covariance model (CM) for RNA family. Returns CM file in Infernal format, which captures both sequence and structure conservation. Can be used with Infernal tools (cmsearch, cmalign, cmbuild) for RNA sequence analysis. Use for: homology searches, structural alignment, custom RNA annotation, sequence classification. CMs are more sensitive than profile HMMs for structured RNAs.

family_id.description: Required: Rfam accession or family name

tools.name: Rfam_get_family
tools.summary: Returns Rfam family metadata: RNA type, sequence counts, species coverage and search parameters.
tools.description: Get comprehensive RNA family information from Rfam database. Returns family metadata including description, curation details, RNA type (snoRNA, miRNA, tRNA, etc.), number of sequences, species coverage, search parameters, and structure source. Rfam v15.1 contains 4,227 RNA families. Query by RF accession (e.g., RF00360) or family name (e.g., snoZ107_R87). Use for: RNA family discovery, understanding RNA function, checking curation quality, identifying RNA types. Available formats: json, xml.

family_id.description: Required: Rfam accession (e.g., RF00360) or family name (e.g., snoZ107_R87)

format.description: Output format

tools.name: Rfam_get_sequence_regions
tools.summary: Lists genomic regions (sequence IDs, coordinates, scores) containing Rfam family members.
tools.description: Get list of all genomic regions containing RNA family members. Returns tab-delimited data with sequence IDs, coordinates, scores, and species. Shows where family is found across genomes. Warning: Some large families return 403 error due to too many regions. Use for: genome annotation, identifying RNA locations, cross-species comparisons, coverage analysis. Available formats: text (tab-delimited), json, xml.

family_id.description: Required: Rfam accession or family name

format.description: Output format

tools.name: Rfam_get_tree_data
tools.summary: Returns the NHX phylogenetic tree for an Rfam family seed alignment.
tools.description: Get phylogenetic tree for RNA family in NHX format (New Hampshire eXtended). Returns tree structure based on seed alignment showing evolutionary relationships. Tree includes species names and sequence information. Can be visualized with tree viewers (FigTree, iTOL, ETE). Use for: phylogenetic analysis, understanding RNA family evolution, species distribution analysis, taxonomic studies. NHX format includes extended annotations beyond standard Newick.

family_id.description: Required: Rfam accession or family name

tools.name: Rfam_id_to_accession
tools.summary: Converts an Rfam family ID/name to its RF accession.
tools.description: Convert Rfam family ID/name to accession. Takes family name (e.g., snoZ107_R87) and returns RF accession (e.g., RF00360). Simple ID conversion utility. Use for: getting stable identifiers, cross-referencing, data integration, creating accession-based links. Accessions are stable across Rfam versions.

tools.name: Rfam_search_sequence
tools.summary: Searches an RNA sequence against all Rfam families with Infernal cmscan.
tools.description: Search RNA sequence against all Rfam families using Infernal cmscan. Submits sequence to batch search server, polls for completion, and returns hits with family matches, positions, scores, and E-values. Typically completes in 4-5 seconds for short sequences. Results available for 1 week. Use for: annotating novel RNA sequences, identifying RNA family membership, finding conserved elements, structural RNA discovery. Returns family IDs, alignment details, and significance scores.

sequence.description: Required: RNA sequence to search (can be multi-line, no FASTA header needed)

max_wait_seconds.description: Maximum time to wait for results (default: 120s). Job continues running if timeout reached.

tools.name: SCP_get_study
tools.summary: Retrieves one Broad Single Cell Portal study by accession with its full description and metadata.
tools.description: Retrieve one Single Cell Portal study by accession, with its full untruncated description. Accessions look like 'SCP1' and are returned by SCP_search_studies and SCP_list_studies. Private or detached studies are not exposed by the public API and will return an error.

tools.name: SCP_list_studies
tools.summary: Lists public Single Cell Portal studies sorted by cell count, optionally filtered by minimum cells or keyword.
