tools.name: compute_prs
tools.summary: Computes a polygenic risk score for one genome VCF against one PGS Catalog model, with optional reference restoration and ancestry.
tools.description:
Compute a polygenic risk score for one genome against one PGS model.

Pass the raw VCF directly; a separate ``normalize_vcf`` call is not needed.
If this VCF has a fresh normalized cache, it is reused automatically;
``genotypes_path`` is the explicit Parquet fast path. For a trait panel —
one genome or several — use
``compute_prs_by_trait(samples=[...])``, then
``compare_genomes`` / ``build_prs_prompt`` / ``plot_trait_panel``.

**Reference restoration (F15/F22).** ``reference_restoration`` fills a scoring
variant's missing reference allele from the precomputed reference-allele
universe (pulled from HuggingFace on first use) so a locus the sample is
confidently hom-ref at scores as dose-0 instead of being dropped as
unscorable-absent — recovering the ~50% coverage gap on genome-wide WGS
scores. Default ``"auto"`` detects the input: whole-universe restoration for
WGS, the matching chip scope for a genotyping array, off otherwise. Pass
``"off"``, ``"wgs"``, or a chip id (e.g. ``"gsa_v3"``) to force a scope. The
result's ``variants_ref_resolved_panel`` / ``variants_ref_resolved_fasta``
counters show how many loci were recovered.

Set ``infer_ancestry=True`` to also infer and attach the sample's genetic
ancestry (``sample_ancestry``). ``genotype_input_mode`` (``"auto"`` /
``"variant_only"`` / ``"all_sites"``) controls how absent loci are read.

Set ``attach_performance=True`` to embed the score's best published
performance (effect sizes, AUROC/C-index, evaluation ancestry) on the
result in the same call. The result also carries ``detected_genome_build`` /
``build_mismatch`` from the VCF (F4).

**Recommended follow-up:** ``percentile`` then ``absolute_risk`` (disease
traits), or ``build_prs_prompt(kind='score')`` for a reusable LLM write-up.

annotations.title: Compute PRS

tools.name: compute_prs_batch
tools.summary: Starts a job computing PRS for one genome VCF against many PGS IDs using a DuckDB engine and cached normalization.
tools.description:
Compute PRS for one genome against many PGS models.

Pass the raw VCF directly; a separate normalization call is not required.
The tool transparently creates or reuses a collision-safe normalized cache,
then uses the memory-safe DuckDB engine with spill-to-disk. It reuses the
scoring caches across scores. This is still **one genome × many PGS IDs**.
For a trait panel across people, use ``compute_prs_by_trait(samples=[...])``
then ``compare_genomes`` / ``build_prs_prompt``.
Set ``attach_performance=True`` to embed each score's best published
performance on its result in the same pass.

``reference_restoration`` (default ``"auto"``) recovers absent-hom-ref
coverage on WGS/array input — see ``compute_prs``; the reference-allele
universe is resolved once and reused across every score. ``genotype_input_mode``
(``"auto"`` / ``"variant_only"`` / ``"all_sites"``) controls how absent loci
are read.

Returns a ``PRSJob`` immediately. When done, ``result`` is the list of
successful ``PRSResult`` objects. If status is queued or running, poll
``prs_job_status(job_id, wait_seconds=25)``.

annotations.title: Compute PRS (batch)

tools.name: compute_prs_by_trait
tools.summary: Computes all PGS scores linked to an EFO/MONDO trait for one or more genome VCFs and saves an HTML trait report.
tools.description:
Compute the PRS scores associated with a trait for one or more genomes.

REQUIRED REPORT DELIVERY: when html_link is set, your reply MUST include it as a markdown link (for example [Open the interactive trait report](<html_link>)) and explicitly tell the user to open it. This is the primary user-facing result, not an implementation detail. Do not skip the link, merely say the report was saved, fetch it, or paste the HTML. html_link is an HTTP URL when available and a file:// URI on local stdio.

Pass a raw .vcf/.vcf.gz path directly. Do NOT call normalize_vcf first as a prerequisite: multi-score tools transparently create or reuse a safe normalized cache, and single-score tools read the VCF directly. normalize_vcf is only an optional explicit step for custom filters. If list_genomes already shows a normalized Parquet, it can be passed directly.

``trait_id`` may be an EFO or MONDO identifier. ``samples`` is always a
list (one genome is fine): each entry is ``Label=path`` or a bare path;
``.parquet`` is a normalized genotype source. Every genome is auto-saved;
the return carries ``reports``, ``result_paths``, and (when models have
percentiles) the primary ``html_link`` plus transport-specific
``html_url`` / ``html_path`` — the just-prs trait HTML report (same page
as ``prs plot trait -o *.html``).
Pass ``result_paths`` to ``compare_genomes`` (2+), ``plot_trait_panel``,
or ``build_prs_prompt``.

**Profile (curation):** ``profile="all"`` (default) returns the raw
associated panel. ``profile="curated"`` is the interpreted *shortlist* —
it drops toy scores (<10 variants), scores with no performance evidence,
scores below the C_wt coverage floor, and de-dups score families.

``interpret=True`` (default) attaches percentiles/quality per model.
Set ``interpret=False`` for raw scores only — the report then says so.
``reference_restoration`` defaults to ``"auto"``. ``superpopulation``
may be a 1000G code or ``"auto"``. Set ``include_prompt=True`` to also
attach the just-prs LLM prompt covering every genome in this call.

This tool returns a PRSJob immediately. If status is queued or running, call prs_job_status(job_id, wait_seconds=25) until done or failed. Do not start a second identical compute — the server reuses the in-flight job. When done, html_link and result (TraitPRSReports) are on the job. Native multi-score work is isolated in a child process so a DuckDB/Polars crash fails the batch without killing the MCP transport.

annotations.title: Compute PRS by trait (give user html_link)

tools.name: download_sample_genome
tools.summary: Downloads a public sample WGS VCF from Zenodo (or any Zenodo record) and optionally normalizes it to Parquet.
tools.description:
Download a public sample WGS VCF from Zenodo to try PRS without your own data.

Two whole-genome sequencing (WGS) datasets open-sourced by the
just-dna-lite project are pre-configured — download both when you want a
multi-person comparison:

- ``sample="anton"`` — Anton Kulaga's genome (~482 MB, CC0 public domain,
  Zenodo record 18370498, file: antonkulaga.vcf).
- ``sample="livia"`` — Livia Zaharia's genome (~349 MB, CC-BY-4.0,
  Zenodo record 19487816, file: SIMHIFQTILQ.hard-filtered.vcf.gz).

Pass ``record_url`` (e.g. 'https://zenodo.org/records/18370498') to fetch
any other Zenodo record, and ``filename`` to pick a specific file when a
record has several.

The downloaded VCF lands under ``<cache_dir>/samples/`` (or ``output_dir``)
and is a drop-in path for ``normalize_vcf`` / ``compute_prs`` /
``compute_prs_by_trait`` (including ``samples=["Anton=<path>", ...]``).

``auto_normalize`` defaults to ``True``: the download is normalized to a
reusable Parquet in the same call, so ``data`` carries both ``path`` (the
raw VCF) and ``normalized_path`` — a one-call, compute-ready genotype
source with no separate ``normalize_vcf`` round-trip. (Normalization is
idempotent, so a re-download of an already-staged sample is cheap.) Pass
``auto_normalize=False`` to fetch the raw VCF only.

Use ``list_genomes`` to see which genomes have already been downloaded
and/or normalized.

Idempotent: if the target VCF already exists with the size Zenodo
reports, the ~hundreds-of-MB download is skipped and the cached file is
reused; likewise a present Parquet skips re-normalization. ``data`` echoes
``reused_cache`` (download skipped) and ``downloaded_bytes`` (bytes
actually transferred, 0 on a cache hit) so the caller can tell a cache
hit from a fresh fetch. Pass ``force=True`` to re-download/re-normalize
regardless.

Returns a ``PRSJob`` immediately. When done, ``result`` is an ``OpResult``
whose ``data`` carries the local ``path``. Poll ``prs_job_status`` if
status is still running — the download is hundreds of MB.

annotations.title: Download sample genome

tools.name: normalize_vcf
tools.summary: Normalizes a VCF into a quality-filtered genotype Parquet (chr prefix stripped, rsid, GT-derived genotype) as a background job.
tools.description:
Normalize a VCF to a quality-filtered genotype Parquet.

This tool is **optional preprocessing**, not a prerequisite for scoring:
``compute_prs``, ``compute_prs_batch``, and ``compute_prs_by_trait`` accept
raw VCF paths directly. Use normalization when you intentionally want a
reusable Parquet for many later analyses or custom quality filters. Before
normalizing, ``list_genomes`` can show whether a cached Parquet already exists.

Strips the chr prefix, renames id→rsid, computes genotype from GT, applies
optional quality filters (FILTER allow-list, min DP, min QUAL), and writes
zstd-compressed Parquet. The output is a drop-in genotype source for
``compute_prs`` / ``compute_prs_batch`` (``genotypes_path``) and for
``compute_prs_by_trait`` (a ``samples`` entry ending in ``.parquet``), so
each VCF is normalized once and reused. Normalize every genome you plan
to compare; scoring still happens per genome.

Idempotent: if the target Parquet already exists it is reused and the
(slow) normalization is skipped — ``reused_cache=True`` flags the hit.
Custom filters (``pass_filters`` / ``min_depth`` / ``min_qual`` / ``sex``)
always re-run, since the cached Parquet may not reflect them. Pass
``force=True`` to re-normalize unconditionally.

Normalization is the slow step (seconds to minutes depending on VCF size).
Returns a ``PRSJob`` immediately; poll ``prs_job_status`` when status is
running. When done, ``result`` is a ``NormalizeResult``.

annotations.title: Normalize VCF

tools.name: percentile
tools.summary: Estimates the population percentile and z-score of a computed PRS using reference panels, theoretical distribution or AUROC fallback.
tools.description:
Estimate the population percentile (0-100) for a computed PRS value.

Uses the 3-tier fallback: precomputed reference-panel distributions
(best), then a theoretical distribution, then an AUROC approximation.
``superpopulation`` is a 1000G code (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS) and should
match **that genome's** ancestry — when comparing people, call this
once per score×genome (or rely on ``compute_prs_by_trait(interpret=True)``).
Pass ``weight_mass_coverage`` (C_wt) from ``compute_prs`` so a deflated
low-coverage percentile is flagged ``reliable=False`` with a caveat
instead of presented as authoritative. Also returns the true z-score and
reference mean/std used, so absolute risk can be computed without
inverting the percentile.

**Important next step:** for disease traits, feed the returned
``z_score`` directly into ``absolute_risk`` to get the concrete
lifetime probability and risk ratio vs the population average. This is
more informative than the percentile alone.

annotations.title: PRS percentile

tools.name: vcf_metainfo
tools.summary: Detects a genome VCF's build, WGS vs array vs gVCF input type and inferred super-population ancestry.
tools.description:
Detect a genome's build, input type (WGS/array/gVCF), and genetic ancestry.

One call that pairs **WGS-vs-array/gVCF detection** with **population
(super-population) inference**, so before scoring you already know: the
genome build (read from the VCF header), whether the input is whole-genome
sequencing, a consumer genotyping array (and which chip), or a gVCF /
all-sites callset, and the sample's inferred super-population.

Pass ``genotypes_path`` (a normalized Parquet from ``normalize_vcf`` /
``download_sample_genome``) for the fast path, or a raw ``vcf_path``.
Genome-build detection reads the VCF header, so it is only available on the
``vcf_path`` branch.

The result carries ready-to-use recommendations:
``recommended_reference_restoration`` (feed to ``compute_prs`` /
``compute_prs_batch`` / ``compute_prs_by_trait`` as ``reference_restoration``
— though those tools default to ``"auto"`` and derive the same thing) and
``recommended_superpopulation`` (feed as ``superpopulation``). Set
``infer_population=False`` to skip ancestry inference (it pulls a small model
from HuggingFace on first use).

annotations.title: VCF meta-info

tools.name: _dna_batch_predict
tools.summary: Predicts properties of multiple DNA sequences in one batch using a single loaded DNA language model.
tools.description:
Predict multiple DNA sequences using a specific model.

        This tool performs batch prediction on multiple DNA sequences using
        a single model. It's optimized for processing multiple sequences
        efficiently by leveraging model batching capabilities.

        Args:
            sequences (list[str]): List of DNA sequences to predict.
                Each sequence should contain only valid nucleotide
                characters (A, T, G, C). Case insensitive.
            model_name (str): Name of the model to use for all predictions.
                Must be one of the loaded models.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Batch prediction results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'model_name',
                  'sequence_count'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

        Example:
            ```python
            result = await server._dna_batch_predict(
                sequences=["ATCGATCG", "GCTAGCTA", "TTAACCGG"],
                model_name=(
                    "zhangtaolab/plant-dnabert-BPE-open_chromatin"
                )
            )
            ```

        Note:
            Batch processing is generally more efficient than individual
            predictions for multiple sequences, especially with GPU
            acceleration.

tools.name: _dna_interpret
tools.summary: Computes per-token attribution scores for a DNA sequence prediction using Captum methods such as integrated gradients, DeepLift or occlusion.
tools.description:
Interpret model predictions using attribution methods.

        This tool provides model interpretability by computing attribution
        scores for each token in a DNA sequence using various Captum methods.

        Args:
            sequence (str): DNA sequence to interpret.
            model_name (str): Name of the model to use.
            method (str): Attribution method. One of: "lig",
                "deeplift", "occlusion", "feature_ablation",
                "layer_conductance", "gradient_shap", "noise_tunnel",
                "integrated_gradients". Defaults to "lig".
            target_class (int | None): Target class index for attribution.
                If None, auto-selects the class with maximum probability.
            max_length (int | None): Maximum token length for tokenizer.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Interpretation results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'attributions',
                  'tokens', 'method', 'target_class', 'model_name',
                  'sequence'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

tools.name: _dna_multi_model_predict
tools.summary: Predicts one DNA sequence with multiple loaded models in parallel for model comparison or ensembling.
tools.description:
Predict DNA sequence using multiple models in parallel.

        This tool performs prediction on a single DNA sequence using multiple
        models simultaneously, enabling model comparison and ensemble analysis.
        It's particularly useful for understanding prediction consensus across
        different model architectures.

        Args:
            sequence (str): DNA sequence to predict, containing only valid
                nucleotide characters (A, T, G, C). Case insensitive.
            model_names (list[str] | None, optional): List of model names
                to use. If None, uses all currently loaded models.
                Defaults to None.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Multi-model prediction results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'model_count', 'sequence'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

        Example:
            ```python
            # Use specific models
            result = await server._dna_multi_model_predict(
                sequence="ATCGATCG",
                model_names=[
                    "dnabert-2", "nucleotide-transformer"
                ]
            )

            # Use all loaded models
            result = await server._dna_multi_model_predict(
                sequence="ATCGATCG"
            )
            ```

        Note:
            Models are processed in parallel for better performance.
            Individual model failures don't stop the entire operation.

tools.name: _dna_mutagenesis
tools.summary: Performs in silico mutagenesis (substitutions, insertions, deletions) on DNA sequences and scores the effect on model predictions.
tools.description:
Perform in silico mutagenesis on DNA sequences.

        This tool evaluates the impact of sequence mutations on model
        predictions, supporting single base substitutions, multi-base
        substitutions, deletions, insertions, and exhaustive combinations.

        Args:
            sequence (str | None): Single DNA sequence to mutate. If provided,
                it is processed as a one-element list internally.
            sequences (list[str] | None): List of DNA sequences to mutate.
                Either sequence or sequences must be provided.
            mutation_type (str): Type of mutation to perform. One of:
                "single_base_substitution", "multi_base_substitution",
                "deletion", "insertion", "combo". Defaults to
                "single_base_substitution".
            positions (list[int] | None): 0-based positions to mutate.
                Required and must be non-empty.
            model_name (str): Name of the model to use for prediction.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Mutagenesis results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'original_prediction',
                  'mutated_prediction', 'delta', 'affected_positions',
                  'mutation_type', 'model_name'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

tools.name: _dna_sequence_predict
tools.summary: Predicts properties of a single DNA sequence using a specified loaded DNA model.
tools.description:
Predict DNA sequence using a specific model.

        This tool performs single DNA sequence prediction using a specified
        pre-loaded model. It's the most basic prediction operation and serves
        as the foundation for more complex prediction tasks.

        Args:
            sequence (str): DNA sequence to predict, containing only valid
                nucleotide characters (A, T, G, C). Case insensitive.
            model_name (str): Name of the model to use for prediction.
                Must be one of the loaded models.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Prediction results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'model_name', 'sequence'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

        Example:
            ```python
            result = await server._dna_sequence_predict(
                sequence="ATCGATCG",
                model_name="dnabert-2"
            )
            ```

        Note:
            This method handles all exceptions internally and returns
            error information in the response rather than raising exceptions.

tools.name: _dna_stream_batch_predict
tools.summary: Predicts multiple DNA sequences with one model while streaming progress updates.
tools.description:
Stream batch DNA sequence prediction with real-time progress
        updates.

tools.name: _dna_stream_multi_model_predict
tools.summary: Predicts one DNA sequence with multiple models while streaming progress updates.
tools.description:
Stream multi-model DNA sequence prediction with real-time
        progress updates.

tools.name: _dna_stream_predict
tools.summary: Predicts one DNA sequence with a model while streaming progress updates via server-sent events.
tools.description:
Stream DNA sequence prediction with real-time progress updates.

        This tool provides real-time streaming prediction with progress updates
        via Server-Sent Events (SSE). It's designed for interactive
        applications
        where users need immediate feedback on prediction progress.

        The streaming capability is particularly useful for:
        - Long-running predictions on large sequences
        - Interactive web applications requiring real-time feedback
        - Progress monitoring for batch operations

        Args:
            sequence (str): DNA sequence to predict, containing only valid
                nucleotide characters (A, T, G, C). Case insensitive.
            model_name (str): Name of the model to use for prediction.
                Must be one of the loaded models.
            stream_progress (bool, optional): Whether to send progress updates
                via SSE. Defaults to True.
            context (Any | None, optional): MCP Context object for progress
                reporting. Required for progress updates. Defaults to None.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Streaming prediction results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'model_name',
                  'sequence', 'streamed'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

        Example:
            ```python
            # With progress streaming
            result = await server._dna_stream_predict(
                sequence="ATCGATCG",
                model_name="dnabert-2",
                stream_progress=True,
                context=mcp_context
            )
            ```

        Note:
            Progress updates are sent at key stages: initialization (0%),
            model loading (25%), processing (75%), and completion (100%).
            Uses chunk-based timeout that resets after each progress update.

tools.name: _hotspots
tools.summary: Identifies mutational hotspot windows in a genomic region (up to 2 kb from a FASTA) by model in silico mutagenesis and sliding-window aggregation.
tools.description:
Identify mutational hotspot windows for a genomic region.

        Computes hotspots from the model itself (in silico mutagenesis over
        the requested reference slice followed by sliding-window
        aggregation) — never from a precomputed window file. The reference
        sequence is read from a per-call server-side ``fasta_path``.

        Args:
            model_name (str): Name of the loaded model to scan with.
            coordinates (dict[str, Any]): Region to scan, as
                ``{"chrom": str, "start": int, "end": int}`` with 0-based
                half-open coordinates (Python slicing convention). The
                region length is capped at 2000 bases per call.
            fasta_path (str): Server-side reference FASTA path
                (.fasta/.fa/.fa.gz/.fna) containing the chromosome. This is
                an operator-trust-boundary file read, not a client upload.
            strategy (str): Per-base score aggregation, one of "maxabs",
                "min", "max", "mean". Defaults to "maxabs".
            window_size (int): Sliding-window size (bases) for hotspot
                detection. Defaults to 10.
            percentile_threshold (float): Rolling-window percentile above
                which a window is a hotspot (0 < p <= 100). Defaults to 90.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Hotspot scan results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'hotspots' (0-based
                  half-open [start, end) pairs relative to the region),
                  'hotspots_genomic' (absolute coordinates),
                  'window_count', 'coordinates', 'sequence_length',
                  'strategy', 'window_size', 'percentile_threshold',
                  'model_name'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

tools.name: _ism_scan
tools.summary: Runs a bounded in silico mutagenesis scan (up to 2000 bases, 100 reported positions) on DNA sequences with a loaded model.
tools.description:
Run a bounded in silico mutagenesis (ISM) scan on DNA sequences.

        Mirrors the ``dna_mutagenesis`` engine surface with tool-boundary
        input caps so a scan cannot silently expand past the tool timeout:
        sequences are capped at 2000 bases and the requested position list
        at 100 entries per call (single-base-substitution ISM costs 3
        forward passes per base). The engine itself scans every position of
        every sequence — the bound on COMPUTE is the sequence cap — while
        the REPORTED mutated entries are restricted to the requested
        positions. Reduce the inputs or raise ``tool_timeout_seconds`` in
        the server config when a larger scan is genuinely needed.

        Args:
            model_name (str): Name of the loaded model to scan with.
            sequence (str | None): Single DNA sequence to scan. Mutually
                exclusive with ``sequences`` (passing both is a matchable
                error; the single sequence is otherwise processed as a
                one-element list internally).
            sequences (list[str] | None): Non-empty list of non-empty DNA
                sequence strings to scan. Mutually exclusive with
                ``sequence``; an empty list is rejected like missing input.
            mutation_type (str): One of "single_base_substitution",
                "multi_base_substitution", "deletion", "insertion", "combo".
            positions (list[int] | None): 0-based positions of interest;
                validated against every sequence's length and echoed in the
                response. Must be non-empty. The reported mutated entries
                (and the delta averages) are restricted to these positions;
                the engine still scans every position of every sequence, so
                the bound on compute is the sequence cap, not this list.

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: ISM scan results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'original_prediction',
                  'mutated_prediction', 'delta', 'affected_positions',
                  'mutation_type', 'model_name'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

tools.name: _zero_shot_score
tools.summary: Scores zero-shot variant effects with a DNA model for inline chrom/pos/ref/alt variants or a VCF, using a reference FASTA and optional ClinVar filter.
tools.description:
Score zero-shot variant effects (dual-mode, D-04).

        Accepts EITHER an inline ``variants`` list of {chrom, pos, ref, alt}
        objects (pos is the 1-based VCF coordinate; materialized to a
        server-side temp VCF with a fixed sanitized name) OR a server-side
        ``vcf_path`` (.vcf/.vcf.gz, size-capped). Both modes route through
        the SAME ``dnallm.inference.vep.evaluate_vcf`` kernel, so skip
        accounting (skip_counts, skipped, skip_fraction) and the convention
        block are identical and surfaced verbatim in the response.

        Inline variants carry no ClinVar annotation, so they are admitted
        under a pass-through convention (labels "not_analyzed"=1, metrics
        None by construction — see the convention block in the response).
        Pass ``clnsig_filter`` (fields: variant_type, positive_labels,
        negative_labels, star_floor — mapping to ``vep.ClinVarFilter``) to
        override the D-17 defaults, e.g. for non-ClinVar ``vcf_path`` input.
        In inline-variants mode the pass-through sentinel is the mandatory
        base: ``variant_type`` is always ``inline_variant`` (an explicit
        conflicting value is a matchable error naming the required value)
        and the caller's other fields override the sentinel, not the D-17
        defaults — any other ``variant_type`` would exclude every inline
        row as ``non_snv_clnvc``.

        Variant count is capped at 500 per call; sequences are capped at
        2000 bases for the ISM tools. ``fasta_path``/``vcf_path`` are
        operator-trust-boundary server-side file reads, never uploads.

        Args:
            model_name (str): Name of the loaded model to score with.
            fasta_path (str): Server-side reference FASTA path
                (.fasta/.fa/.fa.gz/.fna) for window building.
            variants (list[dict[str, Any]] | None): Inline variants, each
                {"chrom": str (whitespace-free chromosome name), "pos": int
                (1-based), "ref": ACGT str, "alt": ACGT str}. Mutually
                exclusive with vcf_path.
            vcf_path (str | None): Server-side ClinVar-style VCF path.
                Mutually exclusive with variants.
            paradigm (str): "mlm" (log-odds, default) or "clm"
                (delta-log-likelihood).
            context_window (int): Reference bases kept on each side of a
                variant. Defaults to 200.
            clnsig_filter (dict[str, Any] | None): Optional ClinVar
                convention override (see above); ``None`` keeps the D-17
                defaults for vcf_path mode and the pass-through convention
                for inline mode. In inline mode the sentinel
                ``variant_type`` is mandatory (see above).

        Returns:
            dict[str, Any]: Zero-shot scoring results in MCP format:
                - On success: Contains 'content', 'records' (per-variant
                  scores/skips), 'skip_counts', 'evaluated', 'skipped',
                  'skip_fraction', 'metrics', 'convention' (all verbatim
                  from the kernel's VepResult), 'input_mode', 'paradigm',
                  'model_name'
                - On error: Contains 'error', 'isError' fields

tools.name: compile_module
tools.summary: Validates a module spec directory and compiles it into parquet files (SNP weights, annotations, studies, PGS and PGx tables), optionally resolving rsIDs via Ensembl.
tools.description:
Compile a module spec directory into deployable parquet files.

Validates the spec, optionally resolves missing rsid/position via
Ensembl DuckDB, and produces the composed parquet artifact in the
output directory: the SNP core (weights/annotations/studies) when the
module carries variants, plus one parquet per 0.4 table kind present
(pgs, diplotypes, pharm_variants, the binning kinds, ...).

spec_dir.description: Path to the module spec directory.

output_dir.description:
Output directory for parquet files. If not provided,
uses the configured default output directory.

compression.description: Parquet compression codec (zstd, snappy, lz4, gzip).

tools.name: validate_spec
tools.summary: Validates a module spec directory (module_spec.yaml, variants.csv, studies.csv) and returns errors, warnings and stats.
tools.description:
Validate a module spec directory.

Checks YAML structure, CSV row validity, cross-row consistency,
and weight/state directionality. Returns a validation result dict

tools.name: predict_variant_effect
tools.summary: Predicts one variant's regulatory effects per modality (expression, TSS, accessibility, histone, TF binding, splicing) with AlphaGenome, plus AVI from the Atlas.
tools.description:
Predicted regulatory effect of a genetic variant, per modality: the strongest tracks of each scorer (expression, transcription start, chromatin accessibility, histone marks, transcription factor binding, splicing), each with its score, calibrated quantile, gene, tissue or cell type, and assay. From the Atlas the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score is included.

Source: a single-nucleotide variant is answered from the precomputed AlphaGenome Atlas; an indel or multi-nucleotide variant runs live inference (score_variant). Both return the same scorers in the same shape. Chosen automatically, overridable with `source`, and always stated in the result.

The response is a summary, never a full score matrix: ranked rows only, capped at top_n (default 25, max 100) and at 40,000 characters.

Results are AlphaGenome model predictions for research prioritization, not clinical classifications: scores and calibrated quantiles are reported as returned, and no pathogenic/benign call is made.

Example: "Analyze chr19:44908684 T>C with AlphaGenome"

ref.description: Reference allele (A, C, G, T; more than one base for an indel)

alt.description: Alternate allele (A, C, G, T; more than one base for an indel)

output_types.description: Optional: modalities to report (default: one scorer per modality)

source.description: Optional: where the answer comes from (default: auto). auto = the precomputed AlphaGenome Atlas for single-nucleotide substitutions, live inference for everything else (indels, multi-nucleotide variants); falls back to live only when the Atlas does not hold the variant. atlas = Atlas only, errors instead of falling back. live = always run the model. The result always states which source answered.

scorers.description: Optional: scorer names to use instead of the defaults. Names come from atlas_list_scorers and are the same for both sources, except the AVI scorers, which the Atlas alone serves.

tools.name: allele_frequency
tools.summary: Returns gnomAD allele frequencies for ClinVar- or AlphaMissense-flagged variants at a genomic position or region.
tools.description:
How common is a variant? Returns gnomAD allele frequencies for variants at a position/region
    ('chr1:55052000' or 'chr1:55050000-55060000'). Low gnomad_af = rare. Frequencies are carried for
    the variants where rarity is informative — those ClinVar has classified or AlphaMissense calls
    pathogenic; other variants return a null gnomad_af rather than a frequency.

tools.name: ancestry
tools.summary: Returns estimated continental ancestry proportions and PCA placement of the loaded genome versus 1000 Genomes and HGDP.
tools.description:
Estimated biogeographic ancestry: continental proportions (k-NN over 1000 Genomes + HGDP) and the
    PCA placement. Continental ancestry is reliable; finer/admixed breakdowns are approximate.
    Requires `locus ancestry` to have run.

tools.name: ask_about
tools.summary: Reports this genome's genotypes at listed rsIDs or its carried GWAS associations for a named condition or trait.
tools.description:
On-demand: given a condition/trait name OR a paper's rsIDs (space/comma-separated), report what
    THIS genome carries. rsIDs → live genotype lookup at those positions (hom-ref-aware) plus any
    ClinVar/AlphaMissense we already have; a trait name → your carried GWAS associations for it. This is
    the 'keep up with new studies' tool: paste rsIDs from a new paper to see your genotypes. Weak
    single-variant evidence — informational, not diagnostic.

tools.name: carrier_status
tools.summary: Reports which curated recessive conditions the genome carries one pathogenic copy of, plus a not-assessed list.
tools.description:
Carrier status for common recessive conditions — which ones this person carries ONE
    pathogenic copy of. This is about their children, not their own health: a carrier is
    typically unaffected. It matters when both partners carry the same condition (1-in-4 risk per
    pregnancy), so frame results around family planning and a genetic counselor, never as a
    personal diagnosis. 'likely_affected' = two pathogenic copies (phase unknown from a VCF, so a
    compound-het is presumed, not proven).

    IMPORTANT: always report the `not_assessed` list alongside any result. This is a curated panel
    of VCF-assessable conditions, not a clinical carrier screen — and several of the most
    important screens (SMN1/spinal muscular atrophy, FMR1/Fragile X) CANNOT be answered from this
    data at all. An empty `hits` list is NOT a negative carrier screen; do not present it as one.

tools.name: clinical_findings
tools.summary: Lists ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic or other-significance variants in the loaded genome, filterable by gene.
tools.description:
ClinVar clinical findings in this genome. With no args, returns pathogenic / likely-pathogenic
    variants. Optionally filter by `gene` (HGNC symbol) and/or `significance` substring
    (e.g. 'pathogenic', 'risk_factor', 'drug_response'). Always confirm health-relevant hits clinically.

tools.name: gene_disease_validity
tools.summary: Returns ClinGen expert-curated gene-disease validity classifications (Definitive to Refuted) for a gene symbol.
tools.description:
Is a GENE itself established as causing disease? Returns ClinGen's expert-curated
    gene-disease validity classifications for a gene (Definitive → Strong → Moderate → Limited →
    Disputed → Refuted), strongest first. Use this to judge whether a gene *matters* — distinct
    from whether a specific variant is pathogenic (that's `clinical_findings`/`variant_dossier`).

    A "Definitive" link means the gene-disease relationship is real; it does NOT mean the person's
    particular variant is pathogenic. An empty result means ClinGen hasn't curated this gene, not
    that the gene is benign. Reads a local file — nothing about the genome leaves the machine.

tools.name: genome_overview
tools.summary: Summarizes the loaded genome: variant counts, genome build and ClinVar/gnomAD/pharmacogenomics annotation coverage.
tools.description:
Summarize the loaded genome: variant counts, genome build, and how much is
    annotated (ClinVar, gnomAD, pharmacogenomics). Call this first to see what's available.

tools.name: gwas_associations
tools.summary: Lists genome-wide-significant GWAS Catalog risk alleles carried by this genome, optionally filtered by trait.
tools.description:
GWAS Catalog risk alleles THIS genome carries (genome-wide significant, p<5e-8), optionally
    filtered by `trait` substring (e.g. 'type 2 diabetes', 'height'). WEAK / EXPLORATORY: single hits
    with tiny effects — do NOT sum them or read them like a calibrated score (use polygenic_risk for
    that). Ordered by significance. Requires `locus gwas` to have run.

tools.name: lookup_variant_by_rsid
tools.summary: Returns the genome's genotype and ClinVar/gnomAD annotations for a dbSNP rsID.
tools.description:
Look up variant(s) by dbSNP rsID (e.g. 'rs1799853'). Returns the genotype and
    any ClinVar/gnomAD annotations carried for that variant.

tools.name: lookup_variants_in_gene
tools.summary: Lists the genome's variants within a gene by HGNC symbol, paginated, using SnpEff annotation.
tools.description:
List variants in a gene by HGNC symbol (e.g. 'BRCA1'). Paginated — pass offset to page.
    `total` is the full match count. Requires the SnpEff annotation step to have run.

tools.name: lookup_variants_in_region
tools.summary: Lists the genome's variants in a chr:start-end region or at a single position, paginated.
tools.description:
List variants in a genomic region. `region` is 'chr7:117480000-117670000' (1-based, chr-prefixed)
    or a single position 'chr7:117559590'. Paginated.

tools.name: pharmacogenomics
tools.summary: Returns PharmCAT star-allele diplotypes, metabolizer phenotypes and CPIC/DPWG drug guidance, filterable by gene or drug.
tools.description:
Pharmacogenomic results from PharmCAT: star-allele diplotypes, metabolizer phenotypes, and
    CPIC/DPWG drug guidance. Filter by `gene` (e.g. 'CYP2C19') or `drug` (e.g. 'clopidogrel').
    Some genes report 'Unknown'/'No Result' — notably CYP2D6, whose calling needs copy-number data
    from raw reads that Locus does not process. Treat those as "not determined", not "normal".
    Requires the PharmCAT annotation step to have run.

tools.name: polygenic_risk
tools.summary: Returns ancestry-matched polygenic risk percentiles for a curated trait set (CAD, LDL, T2D, Lp(a)).
tools.description:
Polygenic (aggregate) risk scores for the curated set (coronary artery disease, LDL
    cholesterol, type 2 diabetes, Lp(a)) — call it to see what is actually scored, reported as
    an ancestry-matched percentile where available. Percentiles are only meaningful within the matched
    ancestry; these are research-grade estimates, not diagnoses. Requires `locus ancestry` to have run.

tools.name: predicted_damaging
tools.summary: Lists rare missense variants unclassified by ClinVar that AlphaMissense predicts pathogenic, optionally by gene.
tools.description:
Rare, predicted-damaging missense variants from AlphaMissense — the 'ClinVar is silent' set:
    variants ClinVar has NOT classified but AlphaMissense scores as likely pathogenic. Optionally
    filter by gene. Use this when ClinVar returns nothing for a gene of interest. These are
    computational predictions, not clinical assertions — far weaker evidence than a ClinVar
    pathogenic call, and most are benign in reality. Rarity filtering is best-effort: gnomAD
    frequencies are only carried for some variants, so a hit is not guaranteed to be rare.

tools.name: run_sql
tools.summary: Runs a read-only SELECT over the genome database tables (variants, cnv, sv, pgx, associations, pgs_scores), capped at 200 rows.
tools.description:
Run a read-only SELECT against the genome database for power queries. Tables: variants
    (chrom,pos,ref,alt,rsid,gt,filter,gene,consequence,clnsig,clndn,clnrevstat,gnomad_af,gnomad_af_grpmax,
    am_pathogenicity,am_class), cnv, sv, pgx_genes, pgx_drugs, meta, traits, associations (carried GWAS
    hits), pgs_scores, ancestry_global, ancestry_pca, watch_findings (the refresh changelog),
    watch_seen_ids, sources. Mutating statements are rejected; results capped at 200 rows.

tools.name: secondary_findings
tools.summary: Reports pathogenic/likely-pathogenic ClinVar variants in the 84 ACMG SF v3.3 medically actionable genes.
tools.description:
ACMG SF v3.3 secondary (incidental) findings: pathogenic / likely-pathogenic ClinVar variants
    in the 84 medically-actionable genes ACMG recommends reporting (cancer, cardiac, metabolic).
    ACMG's recessive genes are reported only when two P/LP variants are present, so single carriers
    are excluded by design. Empty is the common, reassuring result — but it means "no P/LP ClinVar
    variant in these 84 genes", NOT a clean bill of health: it cannot see variants ClinVar hasn't
    classified, non-coding or structural variants, or any gene off this list. Confirm hits clinically.

tools.name: structural_variants
tools.summary: Returns copy-number and structural variant events overlapping a region, with estimated copy number.
tools.description:
Copy-number (CNV) and structural (SV) events overlapping a region ('chr1:1000000-2000000').
    For CNVs, `cn` is the estimated copy number (2 = normal diploid).

tools.name: traits
tools.summary: Reports single-SNP wellness traits, the HLA-B*57:01 proxy and mtDNA maternal haplogroup, filterable by category.
tools.description:
Single-SNP traits/wellness (lactose, caffeine, alcohol flush, earwax, eye color, muscle type),
    the HLA-B*57:01 abacavir-hypersensitivity screening proxy, and the mtDNA maternal-lineage
    haplogroup. Filter by `category`: 'wellness' | 'pharmacogenomic' | 'maternal lineage' (the
    haplogroup lives under the last one). Call with no filter to see everything. Informational,
    not diagnostic. Requires `locus traits` to have run.

tools.name: variant_dossier
tools.summary: Returns all evidence for one rsID in this genome: zygosity, consequence, ClinVar, AlphaMissense, gnomAD, ACMG and GWAS hits.
tools.description:
Everything this genome knows about ONE variant, in a single call: genotype/zygosity, gene,
    consequence, the ClinVar call and its review status, the AlphaMissense prediction, gnomAD
    frequency, whether the gene is ACMG-actionable or on the carrier panel, any carried GWAS
    associations, and a literature link.

    Prefer this over assembling a picture from separate lookups. The evidence types routinely
    DISAGREE and only mean something together — an AlphaMissense "pathogenic" call looks alarming
    until you see ClinVar calls it benign and 40% of people carry it. Precedence: ClinVar (with its
    review status) outranks AlphaMissense, which is a prediction and never overrides a benign call;
    a high gnomAD frequency argues strongly against a severe effect regardless of prediction. If
    the fields conflict, say so rather than reporting the scariest one. A variant not found is
    almost certainly homozygous-reference, not 'ruled out'.

tools.name: variants_in_study
tools.summary: Pulls the variants a GWAS study (by PMID) reported via the GWAS Catalog and genotypes them in this genome.
tools.description:
Given the PubMed ID of a GWAS study, pull the variants it reported (via the GWAS Catalog) and
    show which ones THIS genome carries — live, hom-ref-aware genotyping. Answers 'this new paper
    found N variants, which do I have?'. Weak single-variant evidence — informational, not diagnostic.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.summary: Returns the changelog since the last refresh, e.g. carried ClinVar variants newly reclassified, filterable by date or tier.
tools.description:
What changed about THIS genome since the last `locus refresh` — the deterministic
    changelog (e.g. ClinVar variants you carry that were newly classified pathogenic or
    reclassified). Ranked strongest-first. Optionally filter by `since` (ISO date like
    '2026-06-01') or `tier` ('strong'|'moderate'|'weak'|'info'). Empty if refresh hasn't run.

tools.name: evolve_sequence
tools.summary: Simulates evolution of a starting sequence over generations with mutation rate, population size and selection on a fitness function such as GC content.
tools.description: Simulate evolution of sequences over multiple generations

selectionPressure.description: Selection pressure (0-1), 0 = no selection, 1 = strong selection

targetValue.description: Target value for fitness function (e.g., target GC content)

tools.name: generate_dna_sequence
tools.summary: Generates random DNA sequences of given length and GC content using random, Markov or codon-biased models, as FASTA or plain text.
tools.description: Generate random DNA sequences with specified parameters

length.description: Length of the DNA sequence to generate

count.description: Number of sequences to generate, default is 1

tools.name: mutate_sequence
tools.summary: Applies random substitutions, insertions and deletions to a DNA or protein sequence with a transition/transversion bias for DNA.
tools.description: Apply mutations to DNA or protein sequences

transitionBias.description: Transition vs transversion bias for DNA (default 2.0)

tools.name: simulate_fastq_file
tools.summary: Simulates single- or paired-end FASTQ reads from a reference DNA sequence with coverage, insert size, error rate and quality models (NEAT-style).
tools.description: Simulate FASTQ sequencing reads with realistic quality scores and error models based on NEAT methodology. Implementation inspired by: Stephens et al. (2016) 'Simulating Next-Generation Sequencing Datasets from Empirical Mutation and Sequencing Models.' PLOS ONE 11(11): e0167047. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0167047

referenceSequence.description: Reference DNA sequence to generate reads from

insertSize.description: Mean insert size for paired-end reads (ignored for single-end)

insertSizeStd.description: Standard deviation of insert size for paired-end reads

mutationRate.description: Rate of true mutations to introduce (0-1)

tools.name: simulate_phylogeny
tools.summary: Simulates a phylogenetic tree and evolves a root sequence along it using JC69, K80, HKY85 or GTR models, outputting FASTA, NEXUS or PHYLIP.
tools.description: Simulate phylogenetic tree and sequence evolution

treeStructure.description: Newick format tree or 'random' for random tree

numTaxa.description: Number of taxa for random tree generation

mutationRate.description: Mutation rate per branch length unit

tools.name: sra_download
tools.summary: Launches a download/conversion job for an SRA run accession to SRA or FASTQ using SRA Toolkit or direct HTTP/S3.
tools.description: Launch download/conversion job using SRA Toolkit or direct HTTP/S3.

format.description: Output format - "sra" or "fastq" (default: "fastq")

prefer_direct_http.description: Use direct HTTP download when possible (default: True)

tools.name: sra_files
tools.summary: Retrieves direct FASTQ/SRA file URLs, MD5 checksums and sizes for run accessions via the ENA mirror.
tools.description:
Retrieve direct file endpoints via ENA mirror.

RECOMMENDED LIMITS:
- For download planning: ≤ 50 IDs per call
- For bulk file listing: ≤ 100 IDs per call

FILE FORMATS PROVIDED:
- FASTQ: Compressed FASTQ files (.fastq.gz)
- SRA: Original SRA format files (.sra)
- MD5: Checksums for verification
- File sizes: In bytes for download planning

DOWNLOAD OPTIONS:
- Direct HTTP: Use provided URLs with wget/curl
- ENA mirror: Fast, reliable European server
- Multiple FASTQ files: For paired-end reads (fastq_1, fastq_2)

ids.description:
List of run accessions (e.g., ["SRR1234567", "SRR7890123"])
 Note: Must be run accessions (SRR/ERR/DRR), not study accessions

tools.name: sra_metadata
tools.summary: Retrieves SRA run/study metadata (platform, library strategy, spots, bases, organism) via Entrez esummary.
tools.description:
Retrieve metadata for SRA runs/studies via Entrez esummary.

RECOMMENDED LIMITS:
- For detailed analysis: ≤ 50 IDs per call
- For bulk metadata: ≤ 200 IDs per call
- Use pagination if you have more IDs

METADATA FIELDS RETURNED:
- accession: SRA run/study accession (e.g., SRR1234567)
- title: Experiment title
- organism: Scientific name of organism
- platform: Sequencing platform (e.g., ILLUMINA, PACBIO)
- instrument: Specific instrument model
- library_strategy: Library strategy (RNA-Seq, WGS, etc.)
- library_source: Library source (GENOMIC, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, etc.)
- spots: Total number of spots/reads
- bases: Total number of bases
- study_accession: Associated study accession

ids.description:
List of SRA IDs (UIDs or accessions)
 Examples: ["123456789", "987654321"] or ["SRR1234567", "SRR7890123"]

tools.name: sra_search
tools.summary: Searches SRA runs and studies with Entrez query syntax (organism, platform, strategy, dates).
tools.description:
Search SRA runs/studies using Entrez esearch.

RECOMMENDED LIMITS:
- For exploration: retmax ≤ 50
- For bulk retrieval: Use pagination with retmax ≤ 200
- Maximum supported: 100,000 records per query

SEARCH SYNTAX:
- Organism: "Homo sapiens[orgn]" or "human[orgn]"
- Platform: "illumina[platform]" or "pacbio[platform]"
- Strategy: "RNA-Seq[strategy]" or "WGS[strategy]"
- Combine: Use AND, OR, NOT operators
- Date ranges: Use datetype, mindate, maxdate parameters

term.description:
Search term using Entrez query syntax
  Examples: 
  - "illumina[platform] AND human[orgn]"
  - "SARS-CoV-2[orgn] AND RNA-Seq[strategy]"
  - "breast cancer[all] AND illumina[platform]"

tools.name: bam_stats
tools.summary: Computes summary statistics (mapped/unmapped reads, references) from a BAM or SAM alignment file.
tools.description:
Get summary statistics from a BAM/SAM file.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a BAM or SAM file.

    Returns:
        Alignment statistics: mapped/unmapped reads, references, etc.

tools.name: cpg_density
tools.summary: Computes CpG observed/expected ratio in sliding windows along a DNA sequence and classifies windows as island, shore or open sea.
tools.description:
Compute CpG density (obs/exp ratio) along a DNA sequence using a sliding window.

    CpG observed/expected = (count_CpG × N) / (count_C × count_G)

    Args:
        sequence: DNA sequence string.
        window_size: Window size in bp (default: 100).
        step: Step size in bp (default: 50).

    Returns:
        List of windows with CpG density and classification (island / shore / open sea).

tools.name: export_gene_expression
tools.summary: Extracts expression values for a list of genes across all cells of an AnnData dataset, optionally from a layer.
tools.description:
Extract expression values for specific genes across all cells.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        genes: List of gene names to extract.
        layer: Layer to use (None = .X, 'counts' for raw counts).

    Returns:
        Expression matrix as records (cells × genes).

tools.name: fetch_ensembl_sequence
tools.summary: Fetches a genomic, cDNA or CDS nucleotide sequence from Ensembl for a gene or transcript ID.
tools.description:
Fetch a nucleotide sequence from Ensembl by ID.

    Args:
        ensembl_id: Ensembl gene/transcript ID (e.g. 'ENSG00000012048',
            'ENST00000357654').
        seq_type: 'genomic', 'cdna', or 'cds' (default: 'genomic').

    Returns:
        Sequence with metadata.

tools.name: fetch_gene_ontology
tools.summary: Fetches GO biological process, molecular function and cellular component annotations for a gene symbol via UniProt.
tools.description:
Fetch Gene Ontology (GO) annotations for a gene via UniProt.

    Returns Biological Process, Molecular Function, and Cellular Component terms.

    Args:
        gene_symbol: Gene symbol (e.g. 'BRCA1').
        organism: Organism name (default: 'human').
        max_results: Maximum GO terms to return (default: 50).

    Returns:
        GO annotations grouped by category (BP, MF, CC).

tools.name: fetch_ncbi_gene_details
tools.summary: Fetches NCBI Gene details (name, summary, genomic location, references) for an NCBI Gene ID.
tools.description:
Fetch detailed information about a gene from NCBI Gene by its ID.

    Args:
        gene_id: NCBI Gene ID (e.g. '672' for BRCA1).

    Returns:
        Full gene details: name, summary, genomic location, references.

tools.name: fetch_ncbi_sequence
tools.summary: Downloads a nucleotide sequence from NCBI by accession in FASTA or GenBank format, with optional truncation.
tools.description:
Download a nucleotide sequence from NCBI by accession number.

    Args:
        accession: NCBI accession (e.g. 'NM_007294.4', 'NC_000017.11').
        seq_type: 'fasta' or 'gb' for GenBank format (default: 'fasta').
        max_length: Truncate sequences longer than this (default: 50000).

    Returns:
        Sequence in requested format with metadata.

tools.name: find_differentially_methylated_regions
tools.summary: Identifies differentially methylated regions between two sample groups using a sliding genomic window and a minimum methylation difference.
tools.description:
Identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) between two groups.

    Uses a simple sliding-window approach: for each genomic window, compute
    the mean methylation difference between groups and flag regions where
    |Δβ| ≥ *min_diff*.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the loaded methylation DataFrame.
        group_col: Column identifying sample groups.
        group_a: First group label.
        group_b: Second group label.
        chrom_col: Chromosome column.
        pos_col: Position column.
        meth_col: Methylation column.
        min_diff: Minimum absolute methylation difference (default: 0.2).
        window_size: Window size in bp (default: 1000).

    Returns:
        List of DMRs with coordinates and methylation differences.

tools.name: find_orfs
tools.summary: Finds all open reading frames above a minimum length in a DNA sequence and returns positions and translations.
tools.description:
Find all open reading frames (ORFs) in a DNA sequence.

    Args:
        sequence: DNA sequence string.
        min_length: Minimum ORF length in nucleotides (default: 100).

    Returns:
        List of ORFs with positions, lengths, and translated sequences.

tools.name: gc_content
tools.summary: Calculates GC percentage and base composition of a DNA or RNA sequence.
tools.description:
Calculate GC content of a DNA/RNA sequence.

tools.name: get_marker_genes
tools.summary: Returns filtered marker genes with statistics for a group from prior rank_genes_groups results.

        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        group: Group name to get markers for.
        n_genes: Maximum number of genes to return (default: 20).
        min_logfoldchange: Minimum log fold change filter (default: 0.25).
        max_pval: Maximum adjusted p-value filter (default: 0.05).

    Returns:
        Filtered marker gene list with statistics.

tools.name: get_string_enrichment
tools.summary: Computes STRING functional enrichment (GO, KEGG and others) for a list of genes or proteins.

        organism: NCBI taxonomy ID (default: 9606 = human).

    Returns:
        Enriched functional terms grouped by category.

tools.name: methylation_summary_by_chromosome
tools.summary: Summarizes methylation levels (mean, median, count) per chromosome for a loaded methylation table.
tools.description:
Summarise methylation levels per chromosome.

    Args:

        chrom_col: Column with chromosome names.
        meth_col: Column with methylation values.

    Returns:
        Per-chromosome mean, median, and count.

tools.name: parse_bedgraph
tools.summary: Parses a bedGraph/BED file of genomic intervals with scores and summarizes chromosomes and score distribution.
tools.description:
Parse a bedGraph file (commonly used for methylation tracks).

    Expects 4+ columns: chrom, start, end, score.  Extra columns are kept.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a .bedGraph or .bed file.
        name: Optional dataset name.
        max_rows: Maximum rows to load (default: 500 000).

    Returns:
        Summary with shape, chromosomes, and score distribution.

tools.name: parse_fasta
tools.summary: Parses a FASTA file and returns sequence count, IDs, lengths and GC content.
tools.description:
Parse a FASTA file and return sequence summaries.

    Args:
        file_path: Path to a FASTA file.
        max_sequences: Maximum number of sequences to return (default: 100).

    Returns:
        Sequence count, IDs, lengths, and GC content.

tools.name: parse_methylation_table
tools.summary: Loads a tabular methylation calls file (e.g. Bismark, nanome) with chromosome, position, methylation and coverage columns.
tools.description:
Load a tabular methylation calls file (e.g. Bismark, nanome output).

    Args:
        file_path: Path to TSV / CSV.
        name: Optional dataset name.
        sep: Delimiter (default: tab).
        chrom_col: Column name for chromosome.

tools.name: parse_vcf
tools.summary: Parses a VCF/VCF.gz file, optionally within a region, and returns variant counts, types and sample records.
tools.description:
Parse a VCF file and return variant summaries.

        file_path: Path to a VCF or VCF.gz file.

        max_variants: Maximum number of variants to return (default: 500).

tools.name: plot_dotplot
tools.summary: Generates a dot plot of expression for a list of genes across cell groups.
tools.description:
Generate a dot plot of gene expression across groups.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        genes: List of gene names to plot.
        groupby: .obs column defining groups (default: "leiden").
        title: Optional plot title.

    Returns:
        Base64-encoded PNG image of the dot plot.

tools.name: plot_heatmap
tools.summary: Generates a heatmap of expression for a list of genes across cell groups.
tools.description:
Generate a heatmap of gene expression across groups.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        genes: List of gene names to plot.
        groupby: .obs column defining groups (default: "leiden").
        title: Optional plot title.

    Returns:
        Base64-encoded PNG image of the heatmap.

tools.name: plot_marker_genes
tools.summary: Plots the top-ranked marker genes per group as a matrix plot from rank_genes_groups results.
tools.description:
Plot top marker genes per group as a ranked genes matrix plot.

    Requires rank_genes_groups to have been run first.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        n_genes: Number of top genes per group to display (default: 5).
        groupby: .obs column that was used for DE (default: "leiden").

    Returns:
        Base64-encoded PNG image.

tools.name: plot_methylation_distribution
tools.summary: Plots a histogram of methylation beta values, optionally split by group.
tools.description:
Plot the distribution of methylation values (beta-value histogram).

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the loaded methylation DataFrame.
        meth_col: Column with methylation values.
        group_col: Optional column to split by (overlay histograms).

    Returns:
        Base64-encoded PNG histogram.

tools.name: plot_volcano
tools.summary: Generates a volcano plot of differential expression results for a group with fold-change and p-value thresholds.
tools.description:
Generate a volcano plot from differential expression results.

    Requires rank_genes_groups to have been run first.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        group: Group from DE results to plot.
        log2fc_threshold: Log2 fold change threshold for significance lines (default: 1.0).
        pval_threshold: Adjusted p-value threshold (default: 0.05).
        top_n_label: Number of top genes to label (default: 10).

    Returns:
        Base64-encoded PNG image of the volcano plot.

tools.name: rank_genes_groups
tools.summary: Runs differential expression between groups (wilcoxon, t-test, logreg) and returns top marker genes per group.
tools.description:
Run differential expression analysis between groups.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset.
        groupby: .obs column defining groups (default: "leiden").
        method: Test method — 'wilcoxon', 't-test', 't-test_overestim_var',
            'logreg' (default: 'wilcoxon').
        n_genes: Number of top genes to return per group (default: 100).

    Returns:

tools.name: reverse_complement

tools.description:

    Returns:
        Reverse complement and related info.

tools.name: run_enrichment_analysis
tools.summary: Runs Enrichr over-representation analysis on a gene list against GO, KEGG, Reactome, MSigDB or WikiPathways libraries.
tools.description:
Run over-representation analysis (ORA) on a gene list using Enrichr libraries.

    Args:
        gene_list: List of gene symbols to test.
        gene_set_library: Enrichr library name. Common choices:
            - GO_Biological_Process_2023
            - GO_Molecular_Function_2023
            - KEGG_2021_Human
            - Reactome_2022
            - MSigDB_Hallmark_2020
            - WikiPathway_2023_Human
        organism: 'human' or 'mouse' (default: 'human').
        top_n: Number of top results to return (default: 20).

    Returns:
        Enrichment results with terms, p-values, and gene overlaps.

tools.name: run_gsea_preranked
tools.summary: Runs preranked gene set enrichment analysis using genes ranked from differential expression results.
tools.description:
Run Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using pre-ranked genes from DE results.

    Requires rank_genes_groups to have been run first.

    Args:
        dataset_name: Name of the AnnData dataset (must have DE results).
        group: Group from the DE analysis to use for ranking.
        gene_set_library: Enrichr/MSigDB library name.
        top_n: Number of top results to return.

    Returns:
        GSEA results with normalized enrichment scores.

tools.name: search_clinvar
tools.summary: Searches ClinVar for variants in a gene filtered by clinical significance and returns type and location.
tools.description:
Search ClinVar for clinical variants associated with a gene.

    Args:
        gene: Gene symbol (e.g. 'BRCA1', 'TP53').
        significance: Clinical significance filter — 'pathogenic',
            'likely_pathogenic', 'benign', 'uncertain', or 'all'
            (default: 'pathogenic').
        max_results: Maximum results (default: 20).

    Returns:
        List of clinical variants with significance, variant type, and location.

tools.name: search_ensembl_genes
tools.summary: Looks up a gene symbol in Ensembl and returns its ID, location, biotype and transcripts.

Look up a gene in Ensembl by symbol.

    Returns:
        Gene info with Ensembl ID, location, biotype, and transcripts.

tools.name: search_ncbi_gene
tools.summary: Searches NCBI Gene by symbol, name or keyword and returns IDs with summaries, chromosome and aliases.
tools.description:
Search NCBI Gene database by gene symbol, name, or keyword.

    Args:
        query: Gene symbol (e.g. 'BRCA1'), name, or free-text query.
        organism: Organism filter (default: 'human'). Use common or
            scientific names.
        max_results: Maximum number of results (default: 10).

    Returns:

tools.name: search_ncbi_nucleotide

        max_results: Maximum results to return (default: 10).

    Returns:
        List of matching accessions with titles.

tools.name: spatial_autocorrelation
tools.summary: Computes Moran's I or Geary's C for all genes to identify spatially variable genes.

    Returns:
        Top spatially variable genes with statistics.

tools.name: translate_sequence

tools.name: uniprot_get_disease_associations
tools.summary: Returns UniProt-curated disease associations for an entry with names, acronyms, disease IDs and OMIM cross-references.
tools.description:
Structured disease associations for a UniProt entry. Returns the
    diseases recorded in DISEASE-type comments with name, acronym,
    UniProt disease ID, OMIM cross-reference, description, and the
    annotation note. Critical for clinical interpretation — distinguishes
    a UniProt-curated disease association (literature-anchored) from a
    raw cross-reference. Empty result does not imply disease-irrelevant;
    see Open Targets / OMIM / DisGeNET for population-level evidence.

accession.description: UniProt accession, e.g. 'P04637' (human TP53) or 'P38398' (human BRCA1). Both reviewed (Swiss-Prot) and unreviewed (TrEMBL) accessions are accepted; case-sensitive.

tools.name: uniprot_lookup_variant
tools.summary: Looks up a protein change (e.g. R175H) in a UniProt entry's natural-variant annotations with curated description.
tools.description:
Look up an HGVS-shorthand amino-acid change (e.g. ``R175H``,
    ``V600E``, ``R248*``) in the UniProt entry's natural-variant
    annotations. Returns the matching variant feature(s) including the
    UniProt-curated description (often a disease association). A null
    result here does NOT mean a variant is benign — UniProt only
    annotates literature-described variants; ClinVar / dbSNP carry
    population-level data.

accession.description: UniProt accession, e.g. 'P04637' (human TP53) or 'P38398' (human BRCA1). Both reviewed (Swiss-Prot) and unreviewed (TrEMBL) accessions are accepted; case-sensitive.
accession.title: Accession

change.description: HGVS-shorthand amino-acid change, e.g. 'R175H', 'V600E', 'R248*' (stop). Format: <original residue><1-indexed position><alt residue or '*'>.
change.title: Change

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for a human-readable report with a provenance footer, or 'json' for a machine-parseable structured payload with the same data. Any other value is rejected.
response_format.title: Response Format

tools.name: uniprot_resolve_clinvar
tools.summary: Looks up ClinVar records for the gene of a UniProt entry, optionally filtered by protein change, with significance.
tools.description:
Look up ClinVar records for the gene encoded by a UniProt entry.
    First fetches the entry to extract the canonical gene symbol, then
    queries NCBI eutils ClinVar by gene (and optional protein-change
    filter, e.g. ``R175H``). Returns clinical-significance classification,
    review status, condition list (trait_set), molecular consequence,
    and the protein-change list per record.

    Critical for clinical workflows — UniProt's natural-variant
    annotations stop at literature-described variants. ClinVar carries
    every variant submitted by clinical labs, with curated significance
    classifications. Combine ``uniprot_lookup_variant`` (UniProt side)
    with ``uniprot_resolve_clinvar`` (population side) for a full
    variant-effect picture.

    Calls https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov — declared in PRIVACY.md.

accession.description: UniProt accession, e.g. 'P04637' (human TP53) or 'P38398' (human BRCA1). Both reviewed (Swiss-Prot) and unreviewed (TrEMBL) accessions are accepted; case-sensitive.
accession.title: Accession

change.description: Optional HGVS-shorthand protein change to filter to, e.g. 'R175H'. Leave empty to return all ClinVar records for the gene.
change.title: Change

size.description: Maximum number of ClinVar records to return; capped at 50.
size.title: Size

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for a human-readable report with a provenance footer, or 'json' for a machine-parseable structured payload with the same data. Any other value is rejected.
response_format.title: Response Format

tools.name: uniprot_resolve_orthology
tools.summary: Groups a UniProt entry's orthology cross-references by database (KEGG, OMA, OrthoDB, eggNOG, PANTHER, GeneTree).
tools.description:
Group every orthology cross-reference in a UniProt entry by source
    database (KEGG / OMA / OrthoDB / eggNOG / HOGENOM / PhylomeDB /
    InParanoid / TreeFam / GeneTree / PAN-GO / PANTHER / OrthoInspector).
    Different databases use different inference methods; surfacing them
    side-by-side lets the agent reason about consensus when comparing
    orthologs across species. Pure-Python — no extra HTTP call beyond
    the entry fetch.

accession.description: UniProt accession, e.g. 'P04637' (human TP53) or 'P38398' (human BRCA1). Both reviewed (Swiss-Prot) and unreviewed (TrEMBL) accessions are accepted; case-sensitive.
accession.title: Accession

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for a human-readable report with a provenance footer, or 'json' for a machine-parseable structured payload with the same data. Any other value is rejected.
response_format.title: Response Format
